ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.claim: All these gathers the wrongdoers of 6:123-124 and their human and jinn tempters.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.anchor: besides the devils among human beings, the ones among the jinn too will be gathered there.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.claim: Group of Jinn means Iblis's followers, not the whole jinn community.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.anchor: their supreme leader, are the ones implied.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.claim: Iblis himself was a jinn who deceived Adam and arrogantly defied the command to prostrate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.anchor: He himself, as is known from the Qur’ ān, belonged to the jinn.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.claim: The address alludes to Iblis's threats in 17:62 and 7:16-17 that he would mislead Adam's progeny except a few and make most ungrateful; his figurative descendants docilely fulfilled his plan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.anchor: have a very subtle insinuation to the words of the two afore-cited verses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.claim: Mutual benefit included worship, offerings and vows to jinn deities, changing lawful and unlawful at their behest, and exploitation by soothsayers, magicians, and mediums without reflection.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.anchor: these companions from mankind worshipped these deities, made offerings and vows to them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.claim: Arabs linked jinn with soothsaying, magic, poetic inspiration, every great poet's jinn companion, valleys, travel, settlement, war, peace, and conquest; they even claimed the Prophet had jinn companions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.anchor: the jinn played a very significant role. It was because of the jinn that soothsaying and magic flourished.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.claim: Human devils' statement is a shameful confession and prelude to pleading for forgiveness, but God interrupts before they finish or can apologize.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p119.anchor: God will interject even before their statement is complete, and without giving them a chance to apologize

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.claim: God's immediate verdict that Hell is their eternal abode closes the door to apology, excuses, and forgiveness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.anchor: so they must not try to present excuses; the doors to apology, excuse and forgiveness now stand closed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.speaker: some exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.claim: Some exegetes take eternal to mean a long period, since the exception appears to qualify an eternal stay; Islahi rejects this reading.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.anchor: exegetes. This is because it shows that apparently “eternal stay” in Hell

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.speaker: some exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.claim: To avoid the apparent difficulty, some exegetes take ma as man; Islahi rejects this as contrary to Arabic.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.anchor: In order to avoid this interpretation, some have regarded

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.claim: The exception does not mean Hell ends: once punishment begins, hope, intercession, pleading, repentance, reform, and freedom of will are gone; only God's will remains, whose secrets He alone knows.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.anchor: the exception is not meant to express the fact that the time of stay in Hell will end one day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.claim: This is as far as the Qur'an's words can be taken; further inferences should be judged on their own merits, not attributed to the Qur'an, and eternity is a divine mystery whose disclosed limits people should accept.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p120.anchor: It is not right to regard it to be the purport of the Qur’ān.

FARRA:v1p352/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p352/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p352/r10.claim: The jinn have led many people astray, which is what قد استكثرتم means here.

FARRA:v1p352/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p352/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p352/r11.claim: Humans benefited from jinn by seeking a valley’s lord for protection when alone or fearful after hunting; jinn benefited from the reverence humans showed them and boasted that they ruled both jinn and humans.
FARRA:v1p352/r11.anchor: أن الرجل كان إذا فارق فاستوحش أو قتل صيدا من صيدهم

NAHHAS:v2p93/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p93/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p93/r19.claim: ويوم يحشرهم is accusative under an omitted verb such as نقول; جميعا is circumstantial, and يا معشر الجن is a construct-state vocative.
NAHHAS:v2p93/r19.anchor: نصب بالفعل المحذوف أي ويوم يحشرهم نقول ( جميعا ) على الحال ( يا معشر الجن ) نداء مضاف

NAHHAS:v2p93/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p93/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p93/r20.claim: The best explanation of the jinn-human mutual enjoyment is that jinn delighted in human obedience and humans in following jinn, including fornication and wine; both parties enjoyed one another.
NAHHAS:v2p93/r20.anchor: أبين ما قيل فيه أن الجن استمتعت من الإنس أنهم تلذذوا بطاعة الإنس إياهم

NAHHAS:v2p93/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p93/r21.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v2p93/r21.claim: Another explanation says the jinn enjoyed the humans because people accepted their suggestions.
NAHHAS:v2p93/r21.anchor: وقيل الجن هم الذين استمتعوا من الإنس لأن الإنس قبلوا منهم

NAHHAS:v2p93/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p93/r22.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p93/r22.claim: The Arabic wording is understood as استمتع بعضنا ببعضنا, with the reciprocal pronoun supplied.
NAHHAS:v2p93/r22.anchor: والتقدير في العربية استمتع بعضنا ببعضنا

NAHHAS:v2p93/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p93/r23.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p93/r23.claim: قال النار مثواكم is subject-predicate, خالدين فيها is circumstantial, and إلا ما شاء الله is an exception not belonging to the first clause.
NAHHAS:v2p93/r23.anchor: ( قال النار مثواكم ) ابتداء وخبر ( خالدين فيها ) نصب على الحال ( إلا ما شاء الله ) استثناء ليس من الأول

NAHHAS:v2p93/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p93/r24.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p93/r24.claim: God is wise in their punishment and knows the measure of their recompense.
NAHHAS:v2p93/r24.anchor: ( إن ربك حكيم ) أي عقوبتهم وفي جميع أفعاله

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.claim: In forms such as شهد and لعب, the second radical is still unvowelled while the first keeps its original kasra, as if the second radical had moved.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.anchor: تسكن العين كما أسكنتها فى علم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.speaker: الأخطل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.claim: Al-Akhṭal's line is cited in the pronunciation with شهد and supports retaining the original first-vowel pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.anchor: سمعناهم ينشدون هذا البيت للأخطل هكذا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.claim: نعم and بئس are verbs in origin; the related forms فيها ونعمت preserve that pattern, and some Arabs say نعم الرجل.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.claim: In غزي الرجل, the yāʾ remains rather than changing to wāw because the form was only lightened from an originally vowelled pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماأسكنمنهذاالبابالذيذكرن.anchor: الأصل عندهم التحرك وأن تجرى ياء

ABUDAWUD:4276/r1.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:4276/r1.speaker: أبو مجلز
ABUDAWUD:4276/r1.claim: Abū Mijlaz says Hell is the recompense for intentional killing, while God may pardon; this illustrates 6:128’s exception for what God wills.
ABUDAWUD:4276/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي مِجْلَزٍ، فِي قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏ وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِنًا مُتَعَمِّدًا فَجَزَاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ ‏}‏ قَالَ هِيَ جَزَاؤُهُ

BUKHARI:806/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:806/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
BUKHARI:806/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that on resurrection day people follow what they worshiped and are judged; this parallels 6:128’s gathering and punishment scene, though the report does not mention the jinn-human alliance.
BUKHARI:806/r1.anchor: أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، أَخْبَرَهُمَا أَنَّ النَّاسَ قَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، هَلْ نَرَى رَبَّنَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ

BUKHARI:6573/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:6573/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
BUKHARI:6573/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra narrates the Prophet’s account of resurrection: people follow what they worshipped, are judged at Hell’s bridge, and some monotheists are rescued from the Fire; it echoes this verse’s gathering and judgment but does not interpret it.
BUKHARI:6573/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ أُنَاسٌ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ هَلْ نَرَى رَبَّنَا

SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r1.claim: يوم may depend on an omitted اذكر or on the omitted speech governing the vocative; al-Zamakhshari instead estimates an omitted event: on that day occurred what defies description.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r1.anchor: يجوز أن ينتصب بفعل مقدر فقدره أبو البقاء تارة

SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r2.claim: The Shaykh prefers the proposed parsing over al-Zamakhshari's because his requires deletion of two clauses, including the verb governing the time phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وما قلناه أولى " يعني من كونه منصوبا ب

SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r3.speaker: الزجاج، الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj makes the phrase passive, يقال لهم يا معشر; the Shaykh finds this apt, in keeping with the Qur'anic description that God does not speak to them or purify them.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r3.anchor: وقدره الزجاج بفعل قول مبني للمفعول: يقال لهم يا معشر يوم نحشرهم

SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r4.claim: يوم may also depend on وليهم, understood as: He takes charge of them for what they did and takes charge of them on the day they are gathered.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r4.anchor: لما فيه من معنى الفعل أي: وهو يتولاهم بما كانوا يعملون

SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r5.speaker: بعض النحويين
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r5.claim: جميعا is either a circumstantial accusative or, according to some grammarians, an emphatic expression.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r5.anchor: حال أو توكيد على قول بعض النحويين.

SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r6.claim: Hafs reads يحشرهم with third-person ياء, referring back to ربهم.

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r1.claim: يا معشر is accusative under the omitted يقول or قلنا; with al-Zajjaj's passive صيغة, it is nominative as نائب الفاعل.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r1.anchor: في محل نصب بذلك القول المضمر أي: يقول أو قلنا، وعلى تقدير الزجاج

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r2.claim: معشر means a group; an Arabic line uses it for the people from whom the speaker defends others.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r2.anchor: والمعشر: الجماعة قال: 2056 وأبغض من وضعت إلي فيه

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r3.speaker: النبي
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r3.claim: The Prophet's saying نحن معاشر الأنبياء uses معاشر for a class or group, and states that prophets do not leave inheritance.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r3.anchor: كقوله عليه السلام: " نحن معاشر الأنبياء لا نورث "

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r4.speaker: الأودي
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r4.claim: Al-Awdi's verse uses معاشر as the plural of معشر, for a group who restore what their people have spoiled.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r4.anchor: وقال الأودي: 2057 فينا معاشر لن يبنوا لقومهم

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r5.claim: من الإنس may be a circumstantial phrase: their allies were human.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r5.anchor: في محل نصب على الحال أي: أولياءهم حال كونهم من الإنس

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r6.claim: Alternatively من identifies the kind, since their allies included humans and jinn, with the phrase specifying the human allies.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r6.anchor: لبيان الجنس؛ لأن أولياءهم كانوا إنسا وجنا

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r7.claim: ربنا has an omitted vocative particle.

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r8.claim: The majority read أجلنا in the singular, matching الذي; an alternative has آجالنا plural while الذي remains singular and masculine.

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r9.speaker: أبو علي
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r9.claim: Abu ʿAli treats الذي as generic, with the masculine singular standing for a feminine relative form.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r9.anchor: فقال أبو علي: " هو جنس أوقع الذي موقع التي "

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r10.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r10.claim: The Shaykh instead parses الذي as an appositive, implicitly الوقت الذي; this makes it generic without a mismatch that would prevent an adjectival analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r10.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وإعرابه عندي بدل كأنه قيل: الوقت الذي

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r11.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r11.claim: Al-Farisi makes خالدين a circumstantial accusative governed by مثواكم, which here is a verbal noun meaning your remaining, not a place noun; he rejects al-Zajjaj's locative gloss.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r11.anchor: قال الفارسي: " المثوى عندي في الآية اسم المصدر دون المكان

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r12.claim: Al-Farisi's poetic evidence uses مغار ابن همام as a verbal event; its على complement fits an action rather than a place, supporting his verbal-noun reading of مثوى.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r12.anchor:
ومثل هذا قول الشاعر:
2058 وما هي إلا في إزار وعلقة
مغار ابن همام على حي خثعما

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r1.claim: A second possible governor is an omitted verb, يثوون فيها خالدين, with مثواكم understood as the place of remaining.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r1.anchor: والثاني: أن العامل فيها فعل محذوف، أي: يثوون فيها خالدين

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa proposes the meaning of the possessive construction as the governor; the author rejects this because the meaning of an iḍāfa cannot govern.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r2.anchor: قاله أبو البقاء أن العامل معنى الإضافة

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r3.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r3.claim: The majority take the exception from the immediately preceding clause, النار مثواكم خالدين فيها.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r3.anchor: فقال الجمهور: هو الجملة التي تليها وهي قوله { النار مثواكم خالدين فيها }

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r4.claim: Abu Muslim instead makes the exception from their statement that they reached the appointed term: it excludes those whom God seized before that term for disbelief and error.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r4.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: " هو مستثنى من قوله

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r5.claim: The author rejects Abu Muslim's antecedent: the wording should then be شئت to match أجلت, and the intervening judgment about the fire improperly separates exception from its antecedent.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r5.anchor: أما الصناعة فمن وجهين أحدهما: أنه لو كان الأمر كذلك لكان التركيب إلا ما شئت

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r6.claim: The author also rejects Abu Muslim's interpretation because it assumes two terms, an early term of seizure and a separately appointed term, which he says is disproved elsewhere.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r6.anchor: وأما المعنى فلأن القول بالأجلين: أجل الاخترام والأجل المسمى باطل لدلائل مقررة

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r7.claim: Makkī and Abu al-Baqa in one view call this a disconnected exception: the fire is their abode, except those who believed in worldly life, by analogy with 44:56; the author finds this remote.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r7.anchor: فذهب مكي بن أبي طالب وأبو البقاء في أحد قوليهما إلى أنه منقطع

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r8.claim: Others regard the exception as connected to the addressed pronoun in مثواكم: those among the group who believed in worldly life are excluded; ما can refer to a rational kind or class.

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r1.claim: For this connected reading, ما can apply to a rational class, as in the Qur'anic phrase فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النساء.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r1.anchor: فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النسآء [النساء: 3]

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r2.claim: The connected exception is questioned because the unbelievers' future punishment and believers' past worldly faith do not share the same time of judgment, as ordinary exceptions require.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r2.anchor: ولكن قد استبعد هذا من حيث إن المستثنى مخالف للمستثنى منه في زمان الحكم عليهما

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r3.speaker: الطبري
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r3.claim: Some take the excepted interval as time in the graves; al-Tabari instead makes it the period from resurrection until entry into Hell, since مثواكم need not refer only to the future.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو المدة التي بين حشرهم إلى دخولهم النار، وهذا قول الطبري

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r4.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes the exception as the combined duration in the graves and the period after resurrection before entering Hell.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r4.anchor: هو مجموع الزمانين أي: مدة إقامتهم في القبور

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the exception marks intervals when the damned are moved from Hell to a valley of extreme cold that tears their limbs; they howl and ask to return.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r5.anchor: يخلدون في عذاب النار الأبد كله إلا ما شاء الله إلا الأوقات

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r6.claim: Some identify the exception as monotheist sinners who enter Hell but do not remain there forever; ما applies to a category of rational people, and the author says the exception is real and apparent.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r6.anchor: وقال قوم: " إلا ما شاء الله هم العصاة الذين يدخلون النار من أهل التوحيد

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r7.claim: The author says this is a genuine exception: the apparent meaning is clear and should not be replaced with a figurative threat that presents an unreal event as real.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا استثناء حقيقة، بل يجب أن يكون كذلك.

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the exception as an ironic intensified threat, like a victimized avenger claiming he will relent only if his enemy wishes it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r8.anchor: وزعم الزمخشري أنه يكون من باب قول الموتور الذي ظفر بواتره

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r9.claim: The author rejects al-Zamakhshari's metaphorical account as unnecessary, since the exception has an apparent literal sense.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r9.anchor: قلت: ولا حاجة إلى ادعاء ذلك مع ظهور معنى الاستثناء فيه

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r10.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says the exception is the time they spent in the world before punishment; the author considers this even farther from the preceding readings.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r10.anchor: فجعل المستثنى زمن حياتهم وهو أبعد مما تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r1.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ, followed by al-Zajjaj, interprets the exception as an increase in punishment; another view says an added form of chastisement, readings that work only as disconnected exceptions.

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r2.claim: The Shaykh parses these as a disconnected exception from the implicit verbal noun: they remain in Hell's punishment except for extra torment beyond the torment denoted by fire.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهذا راجع إلى الاستثناء من المصدر الذي يدل عليه معنى الكلام

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says this addresses the Prophet and community, not the Judgment scene: it excludes present unbelievers who God knows will later believe, as indicated by حكيم عليم.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " ويتجه عندي في هذا الاستثناء أن يكون مخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r4.claim: The Shaykh calls Ibn ʿAtiyya's reading good, but notes he had earlier called the direct divine address the apparent reading; no strong clue justifies departing from it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهو تأويل حسن وكان قد قال قبل ذلك

BUKHARI:7047/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7047/r1.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
BUKHARI:7047/r1.claim: Samura reports the Prophet's dream of punishments for abandoning Qur’an and prescribed prayer, spreading lies, adultery, and usury, alongside Abraham among children who died in fitra and forgiveness for mixed deeds; it depicts the Fire's judgment in 6:128.
BUKHARI:7047/r1.anchor: سَمُرَةُ بْنُ جُنْدَبٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِمَّا يُكْثِرُ أَنْ يَقُولَ لأَصْحَابِهِ

BUKHARI:7410/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7410/r1.speaker: أنس
BUKHARI:7410/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's intercession on Judgment Day: those with even a grain of good and testimony to God's oneness emerge from Fire, while those whom the Quran has detained remain; this illustrates the verse's conditional permanence.
BUKHARI:7410/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَنَسٍ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم

BUKHARI:7437/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7437/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
BUKHARI:7437/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's judgment scene: deeds govern passage over Hell's bridge, monotheists are rescued, and the last hell-dweller enters Paradise; Abu Sa'id recalls tenfold reward beyond Abu Hurayra's wording, illustrating the verse's Fire and divine mercy.
BUKHARI:7437/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ النَّاسَ، قَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ هَلْ نَرَى رَبَّنَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ

BUKHARI:7438/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7438/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
BUKHARI:7438/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's judgment scene: deeds govern passage over Hell's bridge, monotheists are rescued, and the last hell-dweller enters Paradise; Abu Sa'id recalls tenfold reward beyond Abu Hurayra's wording, illustrating the verse's Fire and divine mercy.
BUKHARI:7438/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ النَّاسَ، قَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ هَلْ نَرَى رَبَّنَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ

ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r1.claim: The jinn have greatly increased their number from among the humans they led astray.
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r1.anchor: المعنى قد استكثرتم ممن أضللتموهم من الإنس

ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r2.claim: An exegetical report says humans sought a valley's jinn lord for protection while traveling or hunting; jinn benefited when humans acknowledged their power to protect.
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r2.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن استمتاع الإنس بالجن أن الرجل كان إذا سافر سفرا فخاف

ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r3.claim: The wording points to humans accepting the jinn's misleading enticements; only a few people sought refuge with jinn, so that practice is not the main sense.
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r3.anchor: والذي يدل عليه اللفظ - والله أعلم - هو قبول الإنس من الجن ما كانوا يغوونهم به

ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r4.claim: Mathwā means a place of residence or abiding.

ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r5.claim: Khālidīn is accusative as a circumstantial expression: Hell is their abode in a state of enduring residence.
ZAJJAJ:v2p291/r5.anchor: منصوب على الحال، المعنى: النار مقامكم في حال خلود دائم

ZAJJAJ:v2p291#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p291#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p291#2/r1.claim: The exception may exclude the period from their rising from the graves through the gathering and their time being reckoned on Judgment Day.
ZAJJAJ:v2p291#2/r1.anchor: فقال خالدين فيها مذ يبعثون إلا ما شاء ربك من مقدار حشرهم من قبورهم، ومقدار مدتهم في محاسبتهم

ZAJJAJ:v2p291#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p291#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p291#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the exception may refer to kinds of punishment God chooses to add; Zajjaj gives this as another possible reading of the exception.
ZAJJAJ:v2p291#2/r2.anchor: وجائز أن يكون إلا ما شاء الله أن يعذبهم به من أصناف العذاب

ZAJJAJ:v2p291#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p291#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p291#2/r3.claim: God is wise in assigning their recompense and wise in all else.
ZAJJAJ:v2p291#2/r3.anchor: أي هو حكيم فيما جعله من جزائهم، وحكيم في غيره

BUKHARI:7440/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7440/r1.speaker: أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BUKHARI:7440/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's account of the Resurrection: after earlier prophets decline, Muhammad intercedes repeatedly, bringing groups from the Fire into Paradise; this bears on the verse's judgment and fate of sinners.
BUKHARI:7440/r1.anchor: عن أَنَسٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ يُحْبَسُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ حَتَّى يُهِمُّوا بِذَلِكَ

BUKHARI:7440/r2.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7440/r2.speaker: قتادة
BUKHARI:7440/r2.claim: Qatada says intercession releases some from the Fire, but those whom the Qur'an has held are those for whom eternal residence is due; he identifies the promised praised station with this intercession (17:79).
BUKHARI:7440/r2.anchor: قَالَ قَتَادَةُ وَقَدْ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ ‏"‏ فَأَخْرُجُ فَأُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنَ النَّارِ وَأُدْخِلُهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ، حَتَّى مَا يَبْقَى فِي النَّارِ إِلاَّ مَنْ حَبَسَهُ الْقُرْآنُ

BUKHARI:7474/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7474/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BUKHARI:7474/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet reserves his unique supplication to intercede for his community on Resurrection Day, a tradition relevant to the verse's judgment and punishment scene.
BUKHARI:7474/r1.anchor: أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r1.speaker: most commentators
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r1.claim: Most commentators identify the jinn here as evil shayatin and assume those beings are being addressed.
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r1.anchor: According to most of the commentators, the invisible beings (al-jinn) referred to here are the "evil forces" (shayatin) among them, such as are spoken of in verse 112 of this surah.

ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r2.claim: Although ma'shar commonly denotes a community or genus of sentient beings sharing characteristics, that usage is based on the verb for intimate consorting.
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r2.anchor: this term is often used to denote a group or community or genus of sentient beings which have certain characteristics in common: a conventional - and undoubtedly justifiable - use

ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r3.claim: From its primary sense and verbal origin, ma'shar means close associates or family, those who live in intimate communion.
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r3.anchor: in its primary significance, a person's ma'shar denotes those who are on intimate terms or in close communion with him (cf. Lisan al-'Arab: "A man's ma'shar is his family")

ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r4.claim: Asad reads the address as misguided humans living close to evil invisible beings, seduced by verse 6:112's glittering half-truths; 6:130 supports this because apostles are human, never jinn.
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n112/r4.anchor: to my mind, the allocution yd ma'shar al-jinn does not denote, "O you community of [evil] invisible beings" but, rather, "O you who are [or "have lived"] in close communion with [evil] invisible beings": in other words, it is addressed to the misguided human beings

ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n113/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n113/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n113/r1.claim: Wali, plural awliya', primarily means one who is close to another; the human allies were close to the evil unseen beings.
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n113/r1.anchor: It is to be remembered that the primary meaning of wali (of which awliya' is the plural) is "one who is close [to another]".

ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n114/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n114/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n114/r1.claim: The exception means that God may spare them through His mercy; Asad points to 6:12.
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n114/r1.anchor: I.e., unless He graces them with His mercy (see verse 12 of this surah, and the corresponding note).

ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n114/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n114/r2.speaker: some of the great Muslim theologians
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n114/r2.claim: Some theologians infer that sinners' afterlife punishment is limited by God's mercy, unlike paradise's unending bliss, citing 11:107 and prophetic reports; Asad refers to a hadith at 40:12.
ASAD-NOTES:6:128#n114/r2.anchor: Some of the great Muslim theologians conclude from the above and from the similar phrase occurring in 11:107 (as well as from several well-authenticated sayings of the Prophet)

IBNHIBBAN:v1p454/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:v1p454/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:v1p454/r1.claim: After the army’s food supply multiplies, the Prophet says a believer meeting God with both testimonies will be shielded from Hell, contrasting their fate with those assigned to Hell in the verse.
IBNHIBBAN:v1p454/r1.anchor: فضحك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى بدت نواجذه ثم قال

IBNHIBBAN:655/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:655/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:655/r1.claim: Samura reports the Prophet’s dream: rejecting the Qur’an, neglecting prayer, lying, adultery, and usury bring punishments; children, including those of polytheists, are born on fitra, and people mixing good and evil may be pardoned, illustrating judgment beyond this life.
IBNHIBBAN:655/r1.anchor: عن سمرة بن جندب الفزاري قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما يقول

IBNHIBBAN:6464/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:6464/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:6464/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet’s intercession: God grants Muhammad successive limits to remove people from Hell until only those retained by the Qur’an or owing eternal stay remain, relating to the verse’s exception and abiding in Hell.
IBNHIBBAN:6464/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يجمع الناس يوم القيامة

IBNHIBBAN:7355/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:7355/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:7355/r1.claim: The Prophet distinguishes a believer’s private reckoning and forgiveness from the public exposure of disbelievers and hypocrites on Judgment Day, extending the verse’s judgment scene.
IBNHIBBAN:7355/r1.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "يدنو المؤمن من ربه يوم القيامة

IBNHIBBAN:7429/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:7429/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:7429/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that after judgment, monotheists are brought out of Hell and the last entrant is granted Paradise; this bears on the verse’s qualification of abiding in the Fire.
IBNHIBBAN:7429/r1.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "فأكون أول من يجوزه، ودعوة الرسل يومئذ اللهم سلم سلم

IBNHIBBAN:7433/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:7433/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:7433/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that some people remain in Hell as long as God wills, then God has mercy on them and brings them to the lowest Paradise, illustrating the verse’s exception.
IBNHIBBAN:7433/r1.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يكون قوم في النار ما شاء الله أن يكونوا

IBNMAJAH:4153/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:4153/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNMAJAH:4153/r1.claim: Umar recounts that the Prophet comforted him over their poverty, saying that the Hereafter belongs to them while worldly abundance belongs to the Persian and Byzantine rulers.
IBNMAJAH:4153/r1.anchor: حَدَّثَنِي عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ، قَالَ دَخَلْتُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ وَهُوَ عَلَى حَصِيرٍ

IBNMAJAH:183/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:183/r1.speaker: رسول الله
IBNMAJAH:183/r1.claim: Ibn Umar reports that God privately confronts and forgives the believer’s sins, while the unbeliever or hypocrite is publicly exposed, citing the verse about those who lied against their Lord.
IBNMAJAH:183/r1.anchor: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ يَقُولُ

IBNMAJAH:4312/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:4312/r1.speaker: رسول الله
IBNMAJAH:4312/r1.claim: Anas reports that on the Resurrection believers seek relief from Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, then Muhammad intercedes repeatedly and God admits groups within limits He sets.
IBNMAJAH:4312/r1.anchor: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ قَالَ

IBNMAJAH:4312/r2.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:4312/r2.speaker: رسول الله
IBNMAJAH:4312/r2.claim: Anas also reports the Prophet saying that people with even an atom’s weight of good in their hearts and faith in God’s oneness will be brought out of Hell.
IBNMAJAH:4312/r2.anchor: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ قَالَ

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p406/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p406/r1.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p406/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads يحشرهم with yāʾ; the remaining readers use the first-person plural نحشرهم. Al-Fārisī says the two forms convey the same meaning; the yāʾ follows the preceding third-person context, while the nūn is supported by other verses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p406/r1.anchor: حفص عن عاصم ويوم يحشرهم بالياء. وقرأ الباقون بالنون

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p406/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p406/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p406/r2.claim: The temporal phrase يوم depends on an implicit verb of saying (القول المضمر).
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p406/r2.anchor: والنون كالياء في المعنى، والذي يتعلق به اليوم: هو القول المضمر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p269/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p269/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p269/r2.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads يحشرهم with yāʾ; the others use nūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p269/r2.anchor: روى حفص عن عاصم ﴿ ويوم يحشرهم ﴾ بالياء وقرأ الباقون بالنون

NASHR:v1p213/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p213/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p213/r2.claim: The author heard that the recitation of Sibt al-Khayyāṭ was so affecting that a group of Jews and Christians embraced Islam after hearing him.
NASHR:v1p213/r2.anchor: وبلغنا عن الأستاذ الإمام أبي محمد عبد الله بن علي البغدادي المعروف بسبط الخياط مؤلف المبهج

NASHR:v1p213/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p213/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p213/r3.claim: The author names Badr al-Dīn ibn Bakhkhān in Syria and Ibrāhīm al-Ḥakarī in Egypt as the latest reciters he knew to reach the highest level.
NASHR:v1p213/r3.anchor: وآخر من علمناه بلغ النهاية في ذلك الشيخ بدر الدين محمد بن أحمد بن بصخان شيخ الشام، والشيخ إبراهيم بن عبد الله الحكري

NASHR:v1p213/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p213/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p213/r4.claim: The author says mastery of tajwīd comes from training the tongue and repeatedly practicing the recitation received orally, like improving handwriting through practice and a teacher.
NASHR:v1p213/r4.anchor: ولا أعلم سببا لبلوغ نهاية الإتقان والتجويد، ووصول غاية التصحيح والتشديد، مثل رياضة الألسن، والتكرار على اللفظ المتلقى من فم المحسن

NASHR:v1p213/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p213/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p213/r5.claim: Al-Dānī sums up the role of practice by saying that disciplined exercise is the only difference between tajwīd and neglecting it.
NASHR:v1p213/r5.anchor: ولله در الحافظ أبي عمرو الداني - رحمه الله - حيث يقول: ليس بين التجويد وتركه إلا رياضة لمن تدبره بفكه

NASHR:v1p213/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p213/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p213/r6.claim: Correct recitation is not theatrical manipulation of the mouth, jaw, voice, shadda, madd, ghunna, or rāʾ; it should remain easy, sweet, natural, and free of affectation.
NASHR:v1p213/r6.anchor: فليس التجويد بتمضيغ اللسان، ولا بتقعير الفم، ولا بتعويج الفك، ولا بترعيد الصوت، ولا بتمطيط الشد، ولا بتقطيع المد

NASHR:v1p213/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p213/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p213/r7.claim: The author laments that the path to the highest mastery has now closed and asks God for success and protection from diminished ambition and ignorance.
NASHR:v1p213/r7.anchor: وأما اليوم فهذا باب أغلق، وطريق سد، نسأل الله التوفيق

MUSLIM:451/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:451/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSLIM:451/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet’s Judgment narrative: idolaters follow what they worshipped, while monotheists cross the bridge and some sinners are drawn from Hell by mercy; the last man eventually enters Paradise.
MUSLIM:451/r1.anchor: أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّ نَاسًا قَالُوا لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ

MUSLIM:475/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:475/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSLIM:475/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet describing the resurrection’s appeal for relief and his repeated intercession bringing groups from the Fire to Paradise, until only those for whom eternal residence is established remain.
MUSLIM:475/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ

MUSLIM:475/r2.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:475/r2.speaker: قتادة
MUSLIM:475/r2.claim: In Ibn Ubayd’s transmission, Qatada glosses those whom the Qur’an holds back from exiting Hell as people for whom eternal residence has become obligatory.
MUSLIM:475/r2.anchor: قَالَ قَتَادَةُ أَىْ وَجَبَ عَلَيْهِ الْخُلُودُ

MUSLIM:488/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:488/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSLIM:488/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet reserving his one granted supplication as intercession for his community on Judgment Day, offering eschatological context for the verse’s exception in describing enduring punishment.
MUSLIM:488/r1.anchor: أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUSLIM:490/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:490/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSLIM:490/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra tells Kaʿb al-Aḥbar that the Prophet reserved his one granted supplication as intercession for the community on Judgment Day; when Kaʿb asks whether he heard it directly, Abu Hurayra confirms.
MUSLIM:490/r1.anchor: أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ لِكَعْبِ الأَحْبَارِ إِنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ

QIRAAT-ER:6:128:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:128:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:128:3#1/r1.claim: The first-person plural reading says We gather them rather than He gathers them, changing narration about God into direct divine speech.
QIRAAT-ER:6:128:3#1/r1.anchor: shifts from narrative about God to God speaking directly

AZRAQI:v1p57/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p57/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
AZRAQI:v1p57/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jurhum travelers from Syria discover Zamzam by seeing birds over the water, obtain Hagar's permission to settle, and later marry the grown Ismail to a Jurhum woman.
AZRAQI:v1p57/r1.anchor: حدثني جدي عن مسلم بن خالد الزنجي عن ابن جريج عن كثير بن كثير عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال لما أخرج الله ماء زمزم

AZRAQI:v1p57/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p57/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
AZRAQI:v1p57/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq's account in Kitāb al-Mubtada names Ismail's first wife as ʿAmāra, daughter of Saʿid ibn Usama.
AZRAQI:v1p57/r2.anchor: عن عباد بن سلمة عن محمد بن إسحاق اسم امرأة إسماعيل عمارة بنت سعيد بن أسامة

AZRAQI:v1p57/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p57/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
AZRAQI:v1p57/r3.claim: Abraham visits from Syria and finds Ismail away; he tells the first wife to change the household's threshold, and Ismail takes this as an instruction to divorce her and sends her back to her family.
AZRAQI:v1p57/r3.anchor: قال إسماعيل أنت عتبة بيتي فارجعي إلى أهلك فردها إسماعيل إلى أهلها فانكحوه امرأة أخرى

AZRAQI:v1p57/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p57/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
AZRAQI:v1p57/r4.claim: Abraham's later wife welcomes him and serves meat and water; he prays for blessing in both and instructs Ismail to keep this good household.
AZRAQI:v1p57/r4.anchor: قال بارك الله لكم في اللحم والماء قال ابن عباس يقول رسول الله

AZRAQI:v1p57/r5.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p57/r5.speaker: رسول الله
AZRAQI:v1p57/r5.claim: The Prophet says that if the wife had offered grain, Abraham would have prayed for blessing in it too, and Mecca would have become a cultivated land.
AZRAQI:v1p57/r5.anchor: يقول رسول الله & لو وجد عندها يومئذ حبا لدعا لهم بالبركة فيه فكانت أرضا ذات زرع

AZRAQI:v1p58/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p58/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
AZRAQI:v1p58/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts Abraham's third visit to Ismail and God's command to build a house at the nearby raised mound where floodwater runs around but not over it.
AZRAQI:v1p58/r1.anchor: حدثنا عبد الله بن عباس قال لبث إبراهيم ما شاء الله أن يلبث ثم جاء الثالثة فوجد إسماعيل عليه السلام قاعدا تحت الدوحة

AZRAQI:v1p58/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p58/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
AZRAQI:v1p58/r3.claim: When the wall rises too high, Ismail brings the Maqām stone for Abraham to stand on; Abraham moves it around the house, giving Maqām Ibrahim its name.
AZRAQI:v1p58/r3.anchor: فلما ارتفع البناء وشق على الشيخ إبراهيم تناوله قرب له إسماعيل هذا الحجر يعني المقام

AZRAQI:v1p58/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p58/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
AZRAQI:v1p58/r4.claim: In another Ibn Abbas report, father and son embrace and weep until birds respond; Ismail agrees to help Abraham build the house.
AZRAQI:v1p58/r4.anchor: فجاء إبراهيم وإسماعيل يبري نبلا له أو نباله تحت الدوحة قريبا من زمزم فلما رآه قام إليه

AZRAQI:v1p58/r5.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p58/r5.speaker: مجاهد
AZRAQI:v1p58/r5.claim: Mujahid says a sakina, a bird, and an angel accompanied Abraham from Syria; its presence explains the tranquility seen on those who circumambulate the House.
AZRAQI:v1p58/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد أقبل إبراهيم والسكينة والصرد والملك من الشام فقالت السكينة يا إبراهيم ربض على البيت

AZRAQI:v1p58/r6.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p58/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
AZRAQI:v1p58/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj describes the sakina accompanying Abraham as having a catlike head and two wings.
AZRAQI:v1p58/r6.anchor: وقال ابن جريج أقبلت معه السكينة لها رأس كرأس الهرة وجناحان

AZRAQI:v1p80/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p80/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
AZRAQI:v1p80/r1.claim: Umar warns Quraysh that Tasm and then Jurhum lost custody of the sanctuary because they neglected its rights and profaned its sacredness; Quraysh must honor it.
AZRAQI:v1p80/r1.anchor: عن قتادة أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال لقريش إنه كان ولاة هذا البيت قبلكم طسم فاستخفوا بحقه

AZRAQI:v1p80/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p80/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
AZRAQI:v1p80/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Ismail had twelve sons by al-Sayyida daughter of Mudad ibn Amr; Nabit and Qaydar became the principal ancestors from whom Arabs spread.
AZRAQI:v1p80/r2.anchor: أخبرني ابن إسحاق قال ولد لإسماعيل بن إبراهيم عليهما السلام إثني عشر رجلا وأمهم السيدة بنت مضاض بن عمرو

AZRAQI:v1p80/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p80/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
AZRAQI:v1p80/r3.claim: Ismail is said to have died aged 130 and to have been buried with Hagar in the Hijr; Nabit succeeded him in custody of the House.
AZRAQI:v1p80/r3.anchor: وكان عمر إسماعيل فيما يذكرون ثلاثين وماية سنة فمن ناب بن إسماعيل وقيدار ابن إسماعيل نشر الله العرب

AZRAQI:v1p80/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p80/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
AZRAQI:v1p80/r4.claim: After Nabit, his maternal grandfather Mudad ibn Amr al-Jurhumi took custody and united Nabit's and Ismail's descendants under their Jurhum relatives.
AZRAQI:v1p80/r4.anchor: فولي البيت بعده مضاض بن عمرو الجرهمي وهو جد نابت بن إسماعيل أبو أمه وضم بني نابت بن إسماعيل

AZRAQI:v1p80/r5.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p80/r5.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p80/r5.claim: Jurhum and Qatura migrated from Yemen under their kings, settled in Mecca after finding water and trees, and divided the upper and lower town between them.
AZRAQI:v1p80/r5.anchor: فلما نزلا مكة رأيا بلدا طيبا وإذا ماء وشجر فأعجبهما فنزلا به فنزل مضاض بن عمرو بمن معه من جرهم أعلى مكة

AZRAQI:v1p80/r6.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p80/r6.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p80/r6.claim: Mudad ruled Jurhum in upper Mecca while al-Sumaydaʿ ruled Qatura in lower Mecca; each king governed his own people without entering the other's territory.
AZRAQI:v1p80/r6.anchor: وكان مضاض بن عمرو يعشر من دخل مكة من أعلاها وكان السميدع يعشر من دخل مكة من أسفلها

AZRAQI:v1p80/r7.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p80/r7.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p80/r7.claim: The two tribes fought over rule; Mudad's allies included Ismail's descendants, and his force met al-Sumaydaʿ and Qatura at Fadih, where al-Sumaydaʿ was killed.
AZRAQI:v1p80/r7.anchor: فخرج مضاض ابن عمرو من قعيقعان في كتيبته سايرا إلى السميدع ومع كتيبته عدتها من الرماح والدرق والسيوف

AZRAQI:v1p80/r8.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p80/r8.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p80/r8.claim: The account explains the name Qayqaʿan by the clatter of Mudad's spears, shields, and swords as his force marched from there.
AZRAQI:v1p80/r8.anchor: ويقال ما سميت قعيقعان إلا بذلك وخرج السميدع بقطورا من أجياد معه الخيل والرجال

AZRAQI:v1p80/r9.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p80/r9.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p80/r9.claim: The name Ajyad is explained by the fine horses that went out from it with al-Sumaydaʿ.
AZRAQI:v1p80/r9.anchor: ويقال ما سمي أجياد أجيادا إلا لخروج الخيل الجياد منه مع السميدع

AZRAQI:v1p80/r10.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p80/r10.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p80/r10.claim: Fadih is said to be named for Qatura's defeat and humiliation in the battle there.
AZRAQI:v1p80/r10.anchor: فقتل السميدع وفضحت قطورا ويقال ما سمي فاضح فاضحا إلا بذلك

AZRAQI:v1p80/r11.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p80/r11.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p80/r11.claim: After making peace in the upper-Meccan ravine later called al-Matabikh, Mudad fed everyone; the name is explained by the cooking done there.
AZRAQI:v1p80/r11.anchor: فساروا حتى نزلوا المطابخ شعبا بأعلى مكة يقال له شعب عبد الله بن عامر بن كريز

AZRAQI:v1p80/r12.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p80/r12.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p80/r12.claim: The account calls the clash between Mudad and al-Sumaydaʿ the first rebellion in Mecca and says Mudad remembered its killing and unjust struggle for power.
AZRAQI:v1p80/r12.anchor: فكان الذي كان بين مضاض بن عمرو والسميدع أول بغي كان بمكة فيما يزعمون

AZRAQI:v2p39/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p39/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
AZRAQI:v2p39/r1.claim: Ibrahim leaves Hagar and the nursing Ismail at a tree above Zamzam with only a water skin; when she asks who will care for them, he says God, and she accepts.
AZRAQI:v2p39/r1.anchor: قالت له أم إسماعيل إلى من تتركها وولدها قال إلى الله عز وجل فقالت قد رضيت بالله عز وجل

AZRAQI:v2p39/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p39/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
AZRAQI:v2p39/r2.claim: When the water and milk run out and Ismail cries, Hagar searches from Ṣafā to Marwa seven times, crossing the valley at a run; Ibn Abbas says this is why pilgrims perform saʿy there.
AZRAQI:v2p39/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس قال أبو القاسم & فلذلك طاف الناس بين الصفا والمروة

AZRAQI:v2p39/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p39/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
AZRAQI:v2p39/r3.claim: Gabriel strikes the ground with his foot and Zamzam emerges; Hagar contains the water with soil, and the Prophet says it would have become a flowing spring had she left it.
AZRAQI:v2p39/r3.anchor: فاتبعته حتى ضرب برجله مكان البير فظهر ماء فوق الأرض حيث فحص جبريل

AZRAQI:v2p39/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p39/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
AZRAQI:v2p39/r4.claim: Some scholars say Jurhum later profaned the sanctuary, treated the Kaaba's sanctity lightly, and took its offerings; Zamzam then dried up and its location disappeared beneath successive floods.
AZRAQI:v2p39/r4.anchor: فلما استخفت جرهم بالحرم وتهاونت بحرمة البيت وأكلوا مال الكعبة الذي يهدى لها سرا وعلانية

AZRAQI:v2p39/r5.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p39/r5.speaker: عمرو بن الحارث بن مضاض
AZRAQI:v2p39/r5.claim: Amr warns Jurhum that Mecca will not tolerate oppression and predicts their humiliating expulsion; when they ignore him, he secretly buries the Kaaba's golden gazelles and Qala'i swords at Zamzam.
AZRAQI:v2p39/r5.anchor: وقد كان عمرو بن الحارث بن مضاض بن عمرو الجرهمي قد وعظ جرهما في ارتكابهم الظلم في الحرم

AZRAQI:v2p39/r6.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p39/r6.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v2p39/r6.claim: God empowers Khuzaʿa to expel Jurhum and gives them custody of the Kaaba and rule in Mecca.
AZRAQI:v2p39/r6.anchor: فسلط الله عليهم خزاعة فأخرجتهم من الحرم ووليت عليهم الكعبة والحكم بمكة

AZRAQI:v2p39/r7.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p39/r7.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v2p39/r7.claim: Zamzam's location remains unknown for a long time until God guides ʿAbd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim to it.
AZRAQI:v2p39/r7.anchor: وموضع زمزم في ذلك لا يعرف لتقادم الزمان حتى بوأه الله تعالى لعبد المطلب بن هاشم

IBNHISHAM:v1p111/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p111/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p111/r1.claim: After Ishmael died, his son Nābit held the Kaaba’s custodianship for a time; after him, Miḍāḍ ibn ʿAmr al-Jurhumī took charge.
IBNHISHAM:v1p111/r1.anchor: قال: لما توفي إسماعيل بن إبراهيم ولي البيت بعده ابنه نابت بن إسماعيل ما شاء الله أن يليه

IBNHISHAM:v1p218/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p218/r1.speaker: سلمان
IBNHISHAM:v1p218/r1.claim: Salman traded his cattle and sheep for transport to Arabia, but the merchants from Kalb betrayed him at Wadi al-Qurā and sold him as a slave to a Jewish owner.
IBNHISHAM:v1p218/r1.anchor: ثم مات وغيب، ومكثت بعمورية ما شاء الله أن أمكث، ثم مر بي نفر من كلب

IBNHISHAM:v1p218/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p218/r2.speaker: سلمان
IBNHISHAM:v1p218/r2.claim: A man from Banū Qurayẓa in Medina bought Salman and took him there; recognizing the city from his teacher’s description, Salman hoped it was the promised place but was not yet certain.
IBNHISHAM:v1p218/r2.anchor: فابتاعني منه، فاحتملني إلى المدينة، فو الله ما هو إلا أن رأيتها فعرفتها بصفة صاحبي

IBNHISHAM:v1p218/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p218/r3.speaker: سلمان
IBNHISHAM:v1p218/r3.claim: Salman missed news of the Prophet’s mission in Mecca while enslaved; after the migration, his owner’s cousin announced that people at Qubāʾ were gathered around a man from Mecca claiming prophethood.
IBNHISHAM:v1p218/r3.anchor: وبعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فأقام بمكة ما أقام، لا أسمع له بذكر

IBNHISHAM:v1p234#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p234#2/r1.speaker: أهل العلم
IBNHISHAM:v1p234#2/r1.claim: Learned authorities report that before Gabriel came, stones and trees greeted Muhammad as God’s Messenger whenever he walked through Meccan ravines; he saw and heard this until revelation began at Ḥirāʾ in Ramadan.
IBNHISHAM:v1p234#2/r1.anchor: وحدثني عبد الملك بن عبيد الله بن أبي سفيان بن العلاء ابن جارية الثقفي، وكان واعية ، عن أهل العلم

IBNHISHAM:v1p246/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p246/r1.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
IBNHISHAM:v1p246/r1.claim: Some learned authorities say Muhammad and ʿAlī secretly prayed in Meccan ravines; when Abū Ṭālib found them, Muhammad described Abraham’s religion and invited him, while Abū Ṭālib refused to leave his ancestors’ faith but promised protection. ʿAlī affirmed his faith, and Abū Ṭālib urged him to remain with the good he had found.
IBNHISHAM:v1p246/r1.anchor: وذكر بعض أهل العلم أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا حضرت الصلاة خرج إلى شعاب مكة

IBNHISHAM:v2p217#3/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p217#3/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNHISHAM:v2p217#3/r1.claim: Jābir reports that a hard rock obstructed the trench; the Prophet prayed over water, spat into it, and sprinkled it on the rock, which crumbled like a dune so that neither axe nor shovel could resist it.
IBNHISHAM:v2p217#3/r1.anchor: أن جابر بن عبد الله كان يحدث: أنه اشتدت عليهم في بعض الخندق كدية، فشكوها إلى رسول الله

IBNHISHAM:v2p527#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p527#2/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v2p527#2/r1.claim: On the Tabūk journey, hypocrites disobeyed the order not to drink from Wādī al-Mushaqqaq before the Prophet arrived; he cursed them, then prayed over the spring and made it gush so the people could drink and fill their needs. He foretold that the valley would become exceptionally fertile.
IBNHISHAM:v2p527#2/r1.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من سبقنا إلى ذلك الوادي فلا يستقين منه شيئا حتى نأتيه

IBNHISHAM:v2p638#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p638#2/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNHISHAM:v2p638#2/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet identified captured Banū Ḥanīfa leader Thumāma ibn Athāl, ordered kind treatment and food and milk, and repeatedly invited him to Islam; after release, Thumāma bathed and pledged allegiance.
IBNHISHAM:v2p638#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد المقبري عن أبي هريرة أنه قال: خرجت خيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNHISHAM:v2p638#2/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p638#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله
IBNHISHAM:v2p638#2/r2.claim: When Muslims wondered why Thumāma ate little after converting, the Prophet said an unbeliever eats from seven intestines while a Muslim eats from one.
IBNHISHAM:v2p638#2/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين بلغه ذلك: مم تعجبون؟ أمن رجل أكل أول النهار في معى كافر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p218/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p218/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p218/r1.claim: Qatada says the jinn led many people astray, from both jinn and humankind.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p218/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الإنس ﴾ قال قد أضللتم كثيرا من الجن والإنس

MUSNAD-AHMAD:4337/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:4337/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:4337/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet saying some people remain in Hell as long as Allah wills, then divine mercy brings them out into the lowest Paradise, illustrating the verse's exception.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:4337/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون، عن ابن مسعود، - قال حسن: إن ابن مسعود حدثهم، - أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " يكون قوم في النار ما شاء الله أن يكونوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and Ibn Atiyya take the gathered group broadly as jinn and humans, including jinn devils and their human disbelieving allies; Ibn Atiyya cites جميعا as emphasis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r1.anchor: قال معناه الزمخشري وابن عطية، قال ابن عطية: ويدل عليه التأكيد العام بقوله: جميعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r2.speaker: التبريزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r2.claim: Al-Tabrizi says the address implies jinn are included in the pronoun when they are gathered; it may refer only to the two species or to them and other creatures.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r2.anchor: وقال التبريزي: وهذا النداء يدل على أن الضمير في يحشرهم دخل فيه الجن حين حشرهم ثم ناداهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r3.claim: Making يوم depend on the deeds in 6:127 would make the pronoun refer only to the believers, an unlikely reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r3.anchor: ومن جعل ويوم معطوفا على بما كانوا يعملون ويوم نحشرهم فالعامل في الظرف وليهم وكان الضمير خاصا بالمؤمنين وهو بعيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r4.claim: He prefers يوم as a time adverb governed by an implied speech verb: on the day We gather them, We say, O company of jinn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r4.anchor: والأولى أن يكون الظرف معمولا لفعل القول المحكي به النداء أي ويوم نحشرهم نقول يا معشر الجن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's separate implied verb is rejected as requiring the ugly omission of two clauses; taking يوم as an object of اذكر also wrongly removes its adverbial force.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r5.anchor: ومما أجاز الزمخشري من نصبه بفعل مضمر غير فعل القول واذكر تقديره عنده ويوم يحشرهم وقلنا يا معشر الجن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r6.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj supplies a passive speech verb, It is said to them, because he considers it unlikely that God addresses them face to face, citing the statement that God will not speak to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r6.anchor: وقدر الزجاج فعل القول المحذوف مبنيا للمفعول التقدير فيقال لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r7.claim: The call is a public address of notoriety and reproach before the assembled witnesses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r7.anchor: ونداؤهم نداء شهرة وتوبيخ على رؤوس الأشهاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r8.claim: Ma'shar means a group and its plural is ma'āshir; the source cites the prophetic phrase We prophets do not bequeath as usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r8.anchor: والمعشر الجماعة ويجمع على معاشر كما جاء نحن معاشر الأنبياء لا نورث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r9.speaker: الأفوه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r9.claim: Al-Afwah's verse illustrates the plural ma'āshir in the phrase فينا معاشر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r9.anchor: وقال الأفوه: فينا معاشر لن يبنوا لقومهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r10.claim: Here istakthartum means the jinn led many humans astray and made them followers, like someone amassing troops or partisans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r10.anchor: ومعنى الاستكثار هنا إضلالهم منهم كثيرا وجعلهم أتباعهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada explain the phrase as excessive misleading and seduction of humans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة: أفرطتم في إضلالهم وإغوائهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r12.speaker: حفص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r12.claim: Hafs reads يحشرهم with yāʾ; the other seven canonical readers read it with nūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p643/r12.anchor: وقرأ حفص يحشرهم بالياء وباقي السبعة بالنون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r1.claim: The human allies of the jinn are disbelievers among humankind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r1.anchor: وقال: أولياء الجن أي الكفار من الإنس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, and al-Zajjaj describe reciprocal benefit: humans get paths to desires from devils, while devils gain human obedience and help in seduction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r2.anchor: روي هذا المعنى عن ابن عباس وبه قال محمد بن كعب والزجاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say humans sought a valley's jinn chief's protection when camping; jinn boasted that they had mastered humans, who now sought their refuge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا ومقاتل: استمتاع الإنس بالجن قول بعضهم: أعوذ بعظيم هذا الوادي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r4.speaker: الكرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r4.claim: Al-Kirmani reports beliefs that the earth was full of jinn, unprotected people would be afflicted, and hunted animals belonged to jinn as mounts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r4.anchor: قال الكرماني: كانوا يعتقدون أن الأرض مملوءة جنا وأن من لم يدخله جني في جواره خبله الآخرون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r5.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r5.claim: Other views include jinn eating bones and using animal dung as fodder, and humans obtaining aims through charms, service, or cultivating the jinn's affection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r5.anchor: وقيل: في كون عظامهم طعاما للجن وأرواث دوابهم علفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r6.claim: The examples represent forms of mutual enjoyment rather than exclusive explanations; the apparent sense is humans benefiting from jinn and jinn from humans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r6.anchor: فينبغي أن يعتقد في هذه الأقوال أنها تمثيل في الاستمتاع لا حصر في واحد منها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r7.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r7.claim: A different view takes the phrase to mean members of each species benefiting among themselves, humans with humans and jinn with jinn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r7.anchor: وقيل: المعنى استمتع بعض الإنس ببعضه وبعض الجن ببعضه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r8.claim: The majority, including Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi, take the appointed term they reached as death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r8.anchor: والأجل الذي بلغوه الموت قاله الجمهور وابن عباس والسدي وغيرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the reached term as resurrection and gathering.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r9.anchor: وقيل: البعث والحشر ولم يذكر الزمخشري غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r10.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r10.claim: Another view makes the term the limit of their mutual enjoyment; they thereby excuse the jinn's following by invoking God's decree and confess their disobedience, desire, denial of resurrection, and regret.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p644/r10.anchor: وقيل: هو الغاية التي انتهى إليها جميعهم من الاستمتاع وهذا القول منهم اعتذار عن الجن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r1.claim: A variant reads آجالنا in the plural, with the relative pronoun construed in the masculine singular.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r1.anchor: آجالنا على الجمع الذي على التذكير والإفراد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r2.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r2.claim: Abu Ali says the plural is a generic noun, so الذي is used where التي might otherwise be expected.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: هو جنس أوقع الذي موقع التي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r3.claim: He parses the relative clause as apposition, effectively وقت الذي; it is generic rather than an adjective because the forms do not agree.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r3.anchor: وإعرابه عندي بدل كأنه قيل: الوقت الذي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r4.claim: Their admission that they reached the term God appointed is evidence against the Mu'tazilite doctrine of two separate terms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r4.anchor: وفي قوله: وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا دليل على المعتزلة في قولهم: بالأجلين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r5.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says مثواكم means the place where you stay.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r5.anchor: أي مكان نوائكم أي إقامتكم قال الزجاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r6.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r6.claim: Abu Ali parses مثوى as a verbal noun, not a place noun, because it governs the circumstantial خالدين and a place noun lacks verbal force.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r6.anchor: وقال أبو علي: هو عندي مصدر لا موضع وذلك لعمله في الحال التي هي خالدين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj's place noun reading works if an implied verb, they remain, is supplied from مثواكم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r7.anchor: ويصح قول الزجاج على إضمار يدل عليه مثواكم أي يثوون خالدين فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r8.claim: The apparent construction attaches the exception to the clause immediately before it, their remaining in the Fire forever.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا الاستثناء من الجملة التي يليها الاستثناء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r9.claim: Abu Muslim attaches the exception to reaching the appointed term, as an exception for those God killed; Abu Hayyan rejects this for its wording, two-term doctrine, and disrupted syntax.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r9.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: هو من قوله: وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا أي إلا من أهلكته واخترمته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari compares the exception to an avenger's threat to relent only if his victim wishes, a mock offer that intensifies the threat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r10.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أو يكون من قول الموتور الذي ظفر بواتره ولم يزل يخرق عليه أنيابه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r11.claim: In the avenger analogy, the exception appears to offer hope while threatening maximal punishment, and so mocks the one receiving the threat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r11.anchor: فيكون قوله إلا إذا شئت من أشد الوعيد مع تهكم بالموعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r12.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r12.claim: Some read the exception as particular people excluded from the disbelieving addressees, namely people who believed in earthly life; Abu Hayyan objects that their times do not coincide.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r12.anchor: فقال قوم: هو استثناء أشخاص من المخاطبين وهم من آمن في الدنيا بعذاب كان من هؤلاء الكفرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r1.claim: A disconnected exception can cross time boundaries, as in the statement that they will taste no death there except the first death in the world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r1.anchor: كقوله تعالى: لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r2.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r2.claim: Another group takes the exception as sinful monotheists who enter the Fire but are not kept there forever.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: المستثنى هم العصاة الذين يدخلون النار من أهل التوحيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r3.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r3.claim: A group treats the exception as a period of time, differing over which period is excluded.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: الاستثناء من الأزمان أي خالدين فيها أبدا إلا الزمان الذي شاء الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r4.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r4.claim: Al-Tabari identifies the excluded time as the interval from resurrection until their entry into Hell; the wording abode in the Fire does not restrict itself to future time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r4.anchor: فقال الطبري: هي المدة التي بين حشرهم إلى دخولهم النار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari excludes periods when they are transferred from Fire to the torment of freezing cold; a report describes a valley so cold that their limbs separate and they cry to return to Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: إلا ما شاء الله أي يخلدون في عذاب الأبد كله إلا ما شاء الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r6.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r6.claim: Al-Hasan takes the exception as their time in the world without punishment; Abu Hayyan says the same objection applies as to excluding people who believed in the world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: إلا ما شاء الله من كونهم في الدنيا بغير عذاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r7.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r7.claim: Al-Farra says illā means siwā, yielding an exception for whatever increase in punishment God wills; al-Zajjaj approaches this explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء: إلا بمعنى سواء والمعنى سواء ما يشاء من زيادة في العذاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r8.speaker: غيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r8.claim: Another view excludes punishment beyond the Fire's torment, treating the exception as disconnected from an implied verbal noun for punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r8.anchor: وقال غيره: إلا ما شاء الله من النكال والزيادة على العذاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r9.claim: He says the exception apparently completes God's address to the addressees, as the transmitted interpretations of it indicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r9.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا الاستثناء هو من تمام كلام الله للمخاطبين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya's good interpretation makes the exception a present address to the Prophet and community for disbelievers then who God knows will later believe; the next clause supports this sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ويتجه عندي في هذا الاستثناء أن يكون مخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمته

MUSNAD-AHMAD:7717/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7717/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7717/r1.claim: Abu Huraira narrates the Prophet's account of the gathering, judgment, and bridge: some believers are rescued from Hell by God's mercy, and the last entrant receives Paradise.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7717/r1.anchor: قال أبو هريرة: " وذلك الرجل آخر أهل الجنة دخولا الجنة "

MUSNAD-AHMAD:7717/r2.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7717/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7717/r2.claim: Abu Sa'id corrects Abu Huraira's report: the last person entering Paradise is promised ten times the stated reward, not merely its like.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7717/r2.anchor: قال أبو سعيد: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

MUSNAD-AHMAD:7927/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7927/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7927/r1.claim: Abu Huraira narrates the Prophet's account of resurrection, judgment, and crossing Hell: some believers are rescued, and the last entrant receives Paradise.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7927/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، المعنى: أن الناس قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

MUSNAD-AHMAD:7927/r2.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7927/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7927/r2.claim: Abu Sa'id corrects Abu Huraira: the final entrant to Paradise receives ten times the reward, rather than only the amount Abu Huraira remembered.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7927/r2.anchor: قال أبو سعيد: أشهد أني حفظت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله في ذلك الرجل:

MUSNAD-AHMAD:8132/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:8132/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:8132/r1.claim: Abu Huraira reports that Muhammad reserves his answered supplication as intercession for his community on Judgment Day, seeking deliverance by God's will.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:8132/r1.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

MUSNAD-AHMAD:8862/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:8862/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:8862/r1.claim: Abu Huraira reports the Prophet's warning that women would be most of Hell's inhabitants, his approval of Zaynab's charity to Ibn Mas'ud's family, and his explanation of the cited deficiencies through menstruation and testimony rules.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:8862/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم،

MUSNAD-AHMAD:8959/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:8959/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:8959/r1.claim: Abu Huraira reports the Prophet will reserve his answered prayer as intercession for his community on Judgment Day, a plea for mercy beyond the warning of Hell.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:8959/r1.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

MUSNAD-AHMAD:9143/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9143/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9143/r1.claim: Abu Huraira reports the Prophet intends to save his answered supplication for intercession for his community on Judgment Day.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9143/r1.anchor: أن أبا هريرة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

MUSNAD-AHMAD:9303/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9303/r1.speaker: نبي الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9303/r1.claim: Abu Huraira reports that the Prophet will defer his answered supplication to intercede for his community on the Day of Resurrection.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9303/r1.anchor: أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

MUSNAD-AHMAD:10906/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10906/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10906/r1.claim: Abu Huraira narrates the Prophet's account of resurrection and judgment: people follow what they worshipped, the faithful cross or are rescued from Hell, and the last entrant reaches Paradise.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10906/r1.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " فأكون أول من يجيز

MUSNAD-AHMAD:10906/r2.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10906/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10906/r2.claim: Abu Sa'id corrects Abu Huraira's recollection: the final entrant to Paradise is promised ten times the stated reward.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10906/r2.anchor: قال أبو سعيد: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

MUSNAD-AHMAD:11099/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:11099/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:11099/r1.claim: Abu Sa'id reports the Prophet's account: Hell continues asking for more until God fills it, while Paradise remains as long as He wills and receives new creation; this concerns final destinies.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:11099/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

MUSNAD-AHMAD:11740/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:11740/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:11740/r1.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that Hell is filled after repeatedly asking for more, while Paradise remains as long as God wills and then receives new creation.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:11740/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

MUSNAD-AHMAD:12153/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12153/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12153/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's repeated intercession: he will bring from Hell everyone with even an atom's weight of faith, illustrating deliverance by God's will.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12153/r1.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

MUSNAD-AHMAD:13562/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:13562/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:13562/r1.claim: Anas transmits the Prophet's account of repeated intercession: believers are taken from Hell into Paradise, leaving only those whom the Qur'an binds to eternal punishment.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:13562/r1.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r1.claim: يوم is an adverb with an implied governing verb such as اذكر, تقول, or كان ما لا يذكر لفظاعته; alternatively it is the object of an omitted verb such as اذكر ذلك اليوم.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r1.anchor: نصب على الظرفية والعامل فيه مقدر أي اذكر أو تقول

ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r2.claim: The pronoun can refer to the two groups, jinn and humans, or specifically to the unbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r2.anchor: والضمير المنصوب لمن يحشر من الثقلين وقيل : للكفار

ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r3.speaker: حفص عن عاصم وروح عن يعقوب
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r3.claim: Hafs from Asim and Rawh from Yaqub read يحشر with ياء; the other readers use the majestic نون and a shift in person that heightens the scene.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r3.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم وروح عن يعقوب ( يحشر ) بالياء والباقون بنون العظة
