ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r4.claim: The address يا معشر الجن has an omitted verb of saying; معشر means a group united in its affairs.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r4.anchor: معشر الجن على إضمار القول والمعشر الجماعة أمرهم واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r5.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r5.claim: Al-Tabarsi defines معشر as a complete community comprising the various classes of a people, deriving the term from ten as a complete unit.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r5.anchor: الجماعة التامة من القوم التي تشتمل على أصناف الطوائف ومنه العشرة لأنها تمام العقد

ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r6.speaker: بعض الفضلاء
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r6.claim: One definition of jinn includes all immaterial beings hidden from the senses, including angels and devils; another restricts it to such beings other than angels.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r6.anchor: أن الجن يقال على وجهين أحدهما للروحانيين المستترين عن الحواس كلها فيدخل فيهم الملائكة والشياطين

ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r7.speaker: آخرون
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r7.claim: Another classification calls angels the good spirits, devils the evil spirits, and the spirits between them a mixture of good and evil.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r7.anchor: إن الروحانيين ثلاثة أخبار وهم الملائكة وأشرارهم وهم الشياطين وأوساط فيهم أخبار وأشرار

ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r8.claim: Whatever definition is used, the addressees are the evil spirits who lead people astray.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r8.anchor: المقصود بالنداء الاشرار الذين يغوون الناس فانهم أهل الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r9.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r9.claim: They understand the jinn as having caused many humans to go astray, through an ellipsis for their misguidance or by making humans their numerous followers.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r9.anchor: أي أكثرتم من اغوائهم وإضلالهم كما قال ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما ومجاهد والزجاج

ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r10.claim: The expression can mean making humans followers in abundance, as when one says a ruler amassed many soldiers.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r11.claim: The address is a reprimand and rebuke; معشر is used for the jinn because seduction often entails cooperation, unlike the human misled group.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r11.anchor: وإنما ذكر المعشر في جانب الجن دون جانب الأنس لما أن الاغواء كثيرا ما يقتضي التظاهر والتعاون

ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r12.claim: Their human allies are the people who obeyed and followed the jinn; من الإنس either identifies their kind or is an omitted description of them.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r12.anchor: اتبعوهم ( من الانس ( أي الذين هم من الانس أو كائنين منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r13.claim: Humans benefited from jinn who showed them desires and ways to attain them; jinn benefited when humans treated them as leaders and followed them.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r13.anchor: أي انتفع الانس بالجن حيث دلوهم على الشهوات وما يتوصل به اليها والجن بالانس حيث اتخذوهم قادة ورؤساء

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r1.speaker: الحسن وابن جريج والزجاج وغيرهم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r1.claim: These authorities say humans benefited by invoking the jinn when afraid while traveling; jinn benefited from humans' admission that they could protect and shelter them.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r1.anchor: وعن الحسن وابن جريج والزجاج وغيرهم أن استمتاع الانس بهم أنهم كانوا إذا سافر أحدهم وخاف الجن

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b takes mutual enjoyment to mean that each side obeyed and complied with the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب أن المراد باستمتاع بعضهم ببعض طاعة بعضهم بعضا وموافقته لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r3.speaker: البلخي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r3.claim: Al-Balkhi suggests the enjoyment may belong only to humans, who benefited from the jinn.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r3.anchor: وقال البلخي يحتمل أن يكون الاستمتاع مقصورا على الانس فيكون الانس قد استمتع بعضهم ببعض الجن

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r4.claim: Many take the appointed term to mean the Day of Resurrection; al-Hasan, al-Suddi, and Ibn Jurayj take it as death, but the first view is preferred.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r4.anchor: وهو يوم القيامة على ماقاله غير واحد وعن الحسن والسدي وابن جريج أنه الموت والأول أولى

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r5.claim: The humans confess their obedience to devils, pursuit of desire, and denial of resurrection, expressing regret, remorse, and submission; their statement adds no new information.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r5.anchor: اعترافا بما فعلوا من طاعة الشياطين وابتاع الهوى وتكذيب البعث

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r6.claim: Some say only the misguided humans' speech is quoted because the tempters have been silenced and cannot speak.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r6.anchor: الاقتصار على حكاية كلام الضالين للايذان بأن المضلين قد افحموا بالمرة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r7.claim: A reading has آجالنا in the plural and الذي in the singular masculine; Abu Ali explains الذي as a collective or as standing for التي.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي : هو جنس أو وقع الذي موقع التي

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r8.claim: قال begins an explanatory answer to an implied question about what God said then.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r8.anchor: استئناف بياني كأنه قيل : فماذا قال الله تعالى حينئذ فقيل قال

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r9.claim: مثواكم means your dwelling and place of residence, or the source/place of your remaining, depending on whether it is a place noun or verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r9.anchor: أي منزلكم ومحل إقامتكم أو ذات ثوائكم على أن المثوى اسم مكان أو مصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r10.claim: خالدين is circumstantial; if مثوى is a verbal noun it governs the state, but if it is a place noun an implied verb such as تبوؤون is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r10.anchor: حال من ضمير الجمع والعامل فيها ( مثوى ) إن كان مصدرا

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r11.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r11.claim: Abu al-Baqa says the genitive relation supplies the governor for the circumstantial phrase; this is rejected because an attributive genitive relation cannot govern it.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r11.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : إن العامل في الحال على هذا التقدير معنى الاضافة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited for an exception of people God already knew would accept Islam and believe the Prophet; this takes the exception within the quoted speech and ما as referring to people.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه تعالى استثنى قوما قد سبق في علمه أنهم يسلمون

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r13.claim: The Ibn Abbas reading is unlikely because using ما for rational people is uncommon and the contextual fit of this exception is weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r13.anchor: استعمال ما للعقلاء قليل فيبعد ذلك كما يبعد شكول ما تقدم للمستثنى

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r14.claim: One report takes the exception as the time when the damned are moved to a freezing region, where their limbs break apart and they cry to be returned to Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r14.anchor: أنهم يدخلون واديا من الرمهرير ما يميز بين أوصالهم من بعض فيتعاوون

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r15.claim: Another view says they leave the place of punishment before entering Hell when Paradise is opened to them, only to have its gates shut; the author finds post-entry release contrary to verses denying unbelievers relief and doubts the report.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r15.anchor: وقيل : إن لهم وقتا يخرجون فيه من دار العذاب وذلك أنه روي أنهم يفتح لهم أبواب الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r16.claim: A well-known report says people brought near to Paradise smell its fragrance and see its rewards, then are ordered away because they have no share; this occurs before they enter Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26/r16.anchor: المشهور أن المرائين يدنون من الجنة حتى إذا استنشقوا ريحها

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects interpreting the exception as a respite before entry: a connected exception must match the excluded item in time, unlike the proposed future respite.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r1.anchor: رده أبو حيان بأنه في الاستثناء يشترط اتحاد زمان المخرج والمخرج منه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r2.claim: A response says a disconnected exception can allow this reading, as in the exception of the first death in another verse, though the author finds the argument questionable.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r2.anchor: إذا لم يكن الاستثناء منقطعا أما إذا كان منقطعا فانه يسوغ

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj interprets the exception as God's willing an increase in punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r3.anchor: إلى وجه لطيف إنما يظهر بالبسيط

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r4.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Munir explains that they remain in the genus of punishment except for an added intensity reaching its ultimate limit, almost beyond the name of punishment; the author calls this a good explanation and notes support in Ibn Abbas's tafsir.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن المنير : ونحن نبينه فنقول : العذاب والعياذ بالله عز وجل على درجات متفاوتة فكأن المراد أنهم مخلدون

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r5.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r5.claim: Arab usage can call an extreme so intense that it nearly becomes the opposite by the opposite's name; Abu al-Tayyib's verse about generosity nearly turning to stinginess illustrates the idiom.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r5.anchor: والشيء إذا بلغ الغاية عندهم عبروا عنه بالضد كما عبروا عن كثرة الفعل برب

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r6.claim: Another view attaches the exception to God's will to lift punishment: their permanence is contingent on His will, although He could have chosen not to punish or perpetuate it.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r6.anchor: هذا الاستثناء معذوق بمشيئة الله تعالى رفع العذاب أي يخلدون إلى أن يشاء الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r7.claim: The contingent-will interpretation refutes the Mu'tazilite claim that wisdom makes eternal punishment rationally obligatory upon God; the author calls this the sound view.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r7.anchor: وفي الآية على هذا دفع في صدور المعتزلة الذين يزعمون أن تخليد الكفار واجب على الله تعالى بمقتضى الحكمة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r8.claim: The exception may hyperbolically say that permanence lasts until God's will changes, which will not happen, teasing and intensifying the unbelievers' despair.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r8.anchor: المراد المبالغة في الخلود بمعنى أنه لا ينتفي إلا وقت مشيئتة الله تعالى وهو مما لا يكون

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r9.claim: The author rebukes a prominent contemporary who claimed this interpretation was new, saying it appears in multiple earlier places.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r9.anchor: ومن أفاضل العصريين الاكابر من ادعى ذلك الوجه له وانه قد خلت عنه الدفاتر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r10.claim: God is wise in punishment and reward, or in all His acts, and knows the two groups' circumstances and deeds and the fitting recompense, or knows everything.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p26#2/r10.anchor: حكيم ( في التعذيب والاثابة أو في كل أفعاله

ALUSI-FULL:v8p27/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p27/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p27/r1.claim: The closing وصف عليم means God knows the jinn's and humans' states and deeds and their fitting recompense, or knows everything, with those matters especially included.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p27/r1.anchor: بأحوال الثقلين وأعمالهم وبما يليق بها من الجزاء أو بكل شيء ويدخل ما ذكر دخولا أوليا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r1.speaker: حفص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r1.anchor: قرأ حفص: {يحشرهم} بالياء، {جميعا} يعني: الجن والإنس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r2.claim: God gathers jinn and humans together at the gathering place of resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r2.anchor: {جميعا} يعني: الجن والإنس يجمعهم في موقف القيامة فيقول: {يا معشر الجن}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r3.claim: The jinn addressed here are devils.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r3.anchor: {يا معشر الجن} والمراد بالجن: الشياطين، {قد استكثرتم من الإنس}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r4.claim: The devils gained many humans through misleading and tempting them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r4.anchor: {قد استكثرتم من الإنس} أي: استكثرتم من الإنس بالإضلال والإغواء أي: أضللتم كثيرا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r5.claim: Their human allies are people who obeyed the devils.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r5.anchor: {وقال أولياؤهم من الإنس} يعني: أولياء الشياطين الذي أطاعوهم من الإنس،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r6.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says humans sought a valley jinn chief's protection when traveling in desolate country, while the jinn gained prestige because humans sought their refuge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r6.anchor: قال الكلبي: استمتاع الإنس بالجن هو أن الرجل كان إذا سافر ونزل بأرض قفر وخاف على نفسه من الجن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r7.claim: Another view says jinn supplied rumors, magic, soothsaying, and alluring or easy paths to desired things, while humans obeyed them in error and sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r7.anchor: وقيل: استمتاع الإنس بالجن ما كانوا يلقون إليهم من الأراجيف والسحر والكهانة وتزيينهم لهم الأمور التي يهوونها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb explains the mutual enjoyment as each side obeying and agreeing with the other.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188/r8.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب: هو طاعة بعضهم بعضا وموافقة بعضهم [لبعض] (2) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r1.claim: Their appointed term is the resurrection and return to life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r1.anchor: {وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا} يعني: القيامة والبعث،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r2.claim: Mathwa means a place of residence.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r3.claim: The exception is discussed in the same way as the exception in 11:107.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r3.anchor: اختلفوا في هذا الاستثناء كما اختلفوا في قوله: (خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك) (هود، 107) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r4.claim: One view excepts the interval between resurrection and entry into Hell from their eternal stay there.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r4.anchor: قيل: أراد إلا قدر مدة ما بين بعثهم إلى دخولهم جهنم، يعني: هم خالدون في النار إلا هذا المقدار.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r5.claim: Another view makes the exception refer to kinds of punishment: their stay is eternal apart from whatever forms of punishment God wills.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: الاستثناء يرجع إلى العذاب، وهو قوله {النار مثواكم} أي: خالدين في النار سوى ما شاء الله من أنواع العذاب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the exception refers to people God knew would accept Islam and be brought out of Hell; on this reading ma means man.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الاستثناء يرجع إلى قوم سبق فيهم علم الله أنهم يسلمون فيخرجون من النار، و"ما" بمعنى "من" على هذا التأويل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r7.claim: One explanation says God knows whom He excepted and knows the goodness and piety in their hearts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p188#2/r7.anchor: قيل: عليم بالذي استثناه وبما في قلوبهم من البر والتقوى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r1.claim: The time expression is accusative under an omitted 'remember' or 'We say'; the pronoun denotes those gathered from both jinn and humankind.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r1.anchor: نصب باضمار اذكر أو نقول، والضمير لمن يحشر من الثقلين

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم وروح عن يعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r2.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim and Rawḥ from Yaʿqūb read the verb with yāʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r2.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم وروح عن يعقوب { يحشرهم } بالياء

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r3.claim: The jinn worshipped by people here are the devils.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r4.claim: The jinn amassed many humans through seducing and misleading them, or gathered them as followers, as a commander amasses troops.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r4.anchor: أي من إغوائهم وإضلالهم، أو منهم جعلتموهم أتباعكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r5.claim: Their human allies are the people who obeyed the jinn.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r6.claim: Humans benefited from jinn by their directions to desires and how to obtain them; jinn benefited when humans obeyed them and fulfilled their aims.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r6.anchor: انتفع الإنس بالجن بأن دلوهم على الشهوات وما يتوصل به إليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r7.claim: Alternatively, humans sought the jinn's protection in deserts and dangers, while the jinn benefited from humans' admission that they could grant protection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r7.anchor: وقيل استمتاع الإنس بهم أنهم كانوا يعوذون بهم في المفاوز وعند المخاوف

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r8.claim: The appointed term is resurrection; the speakers confess obeying Satan, following desire, and denying resurrection, and regret their state.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r8.anchor: أي البعث وهو اعتراف بما فعلوه من طاعة الشيطان واتباع الهوى وتكذيب البعث

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r9.claim: Mathwākum means either your dwelling or the place that contains your dwelling.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r10.claim: The circumstantial phrase 'abiding therein' is governed by mathwākum if that is a verbal noun; if it means a place, the construction is possessive.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r10.anchor: حال والعامل فيها مثواكم إن جعل مصدرا، ومعنى الإضافة إن جعل مكانا

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r11.claim: The exception may be the periods when they are transferred from the Fire to the intense cold, or a period before entering the Fire, when their entry is delayed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128/r11.anchor: إلا الأوقات التي ينقلون فيها من النار إلى الزمهرير

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128-130/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128-130/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128-130/r1.claim: God is wise in His acts and knows the deeds and states of both jinn and humans.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:128-130/r1.anchor: في أفعاله. { عليم } بأعمال الثقلين وأحوالهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r1.claim: The gathering day is a central, previously veiled subject of the sūra: its opening alludes to it and later passages repeatedly disclose aspects of it.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r1.anchor: فذكر هنا سبحانه بعض أحوال الغافلين

BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r2.claim: God gathers every ally and enemy, leaving no one out.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r3.claim: God addresses the jinn through whichever troops He wills to rebuke and humiliate them when they have no power to defend themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r3.anchor: تبكيتا وتوبيخا حين لا يكون لهم مدافعة أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r4.claim: Here jinn are hidden, fearsome rebellious devils who gain power over humans and see humans from where humans cannot see them.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r4.anchor: المستترين الموحشين من مردة الشياطين المسلطين على الإنس

BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r5.claim: The jinn sought and achieved a multitude of human followers by leading visible, sociable people astray until most became their adherents.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r5.anchor: من إغواء المؤنسين الظاهرين حتى صار أكثرهم أتباعكم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r6.claim: The verse’s paired wording uses paralleled omission: the jinn’s concealment implies human visibility, while human sociability implies the jinn’s eeriness and aversion.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r6.anchor: عبر بما يدل على الستر أولا دلالة على ضده

BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r7.claim: The human allies’ speech is linked to an omitted jinn response, reconstructed from the dialogue elaborated in the following sūra.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r7.anchor: هو عطف على جواب الجن المستتر عن العامل في

BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r8.claim: The past tense presents the dialogue as certain to occur because it is reported by the One who never breaks His promise.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r8.anchor: وذكره بلفظ الماضي إشارة إلى تحقق وقوعه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r1.claim: Biqāʿī relates the exchange to the later followers’ blame of their predecessors in the account of the Fire.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r1.anchor: قالت أخراهم لأولاهم ربنا هؤلاء أضلونا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r2.claim: He also compares it with the weak followers’ admission that they had followed the arrogant.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r2.anchor: فقال الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r3.claim: The human allies are people who followed and obeyed the jinn in the misguidance they summoned them to.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r3.anchor: أي الذين تولوهم بالاتباع والطاعة فيما دعوهم إليه من الضلال

BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r4.claim: They say humans enjoyed the jinn’s claims, while the jinn enjoyed human obedience and the humans’ seeking their protection.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r4.anchor: وهم بنا في طاعتنا لهم وعياذنا بهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r5.claim: By invoking the appointed term they shift responsibility to destiny: both groups reached death’s decree and jointly denied this day, so both deserve punishment.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r6.claim: Hell is the common home of both groups, and appealing to destiny cannot benefit them.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r6.anchor: أي منزلكم جميعا من غير أن تنفعكم الإحالة على القدر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r7.claim: Their punishment has no end because they firmly intended to remain in disbelief forever; recompense matches the deed.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r7.anchor: لأن الأعمال بالنية وقد كنتم على عزم ثابت أنكم على هذا الكفر ما بقيتم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r8.claim: Making the punishment’s duration contingent on divine will affirms that God is not bound by any obligation and that His ownership is complete.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r8.anchor: بين سبحانه أن ملكه ليس كذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r9.claim: Biqāʿī says God will not will any end to their punishment; the contingent wording increases their torment by dangling a hope that has no prospect.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r9.anchor: وقد تقرر أنه سبحانه لا يشاء انقطاع شيء من ذلك عنهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r10.claim: The greatest divine name is used to display majesty and guard the divine station, leaving no one able even to contemplate objection.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r10.anchor: ولما كان القصد في هذه السورة إلى إظهار العظمة

BURSEVI:v3p79/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79/r1.claim: The author prays to be among those on the straight path who reach God's presence with sound hearts and are saved from painful punishment.
BURSEVI:v3p79/r1.anchor: اللهم اجعلنا من الذين سلكوا الصراط المستقيم ووصلوا إلى جنابك بالقلب السليم

BURSEVI:v3p79/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79/r2.claim: The verse tells the Prophet to remind Meccans and others of the day God gathers humans and jinn together at the Resurrection and rebukes them.
BURSEVI:v3p79/r2.anchor: أي : واذكر يا محمد لأهل مكة وغيرهم يوم يحشر الله الثقلين جميعا

BURSEVI:v3p79/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79/r3.claim: Maʿshar means a group held together by a shared bond and association; its plural is maʿāshir, and here the jinn are the devils.
BURSEVI:v3p79/r3.anchor: يا معشر الجن} أي : يا جماعة الشياطين ، فإن المعشر الجماعة التي تضبطهم جهة واحدة

BURSEVI:v3p79/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v3p79/r4.claim: One explanation derives maʿshar from ten as a complete large number, treating a maʿshar as the place of a full multitude.
BURSEVI:v3p79/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : سميت الجماعة بالمعشر لبلوغها غاية الكثرة

BURSEVI:v3p79/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79/r5.claim: Jinn are named for their concealment from people's sight.
BURSEVI:v3p79/r5.anchor: وسمي الجن : جنا لاجتنانهم أي : استتارهم عن أعين الناس

BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r1.claim: The jinn amassed many humans by misleading and leading them astray.
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r1.anchor: {قد استكثرتم من الانس} أي : من إغوائهم وإضلالهم

BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r2.claim: Their allies are the humans who obeyed the devils; من الإنس is a circumstantial phrase modifying أولياؤهم.
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r2.anchor: أي : أولياء الشياطين الذين أطاعوهم حال كونهم

BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r3.claim: Humans benefited from jinn who showed and facilitated ways to satisfy desires; jinn benefited from human obedience, as a ruler benefits from followers' submission.
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r3.anchor: أما انتفاع الإنس بالجن فمن حيث

BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r4.claim: The appointed term is the Resurrection; the admission expresses regret and submission after obeying devils, following desire, and denying resurrection.
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r4.anchor: وهو يوم القيامة قالوه اعترافا بما فعلوا من طاعة الشياطين

BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r5.claim: The Persian verses warn the sleeper to wake before death ends the chance to act: the teacher says they did no work and time has passed.
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r5.anchor: كنون بايد اي خفته بيدار بود ومرك اندر آرد زخوابت ه سود

BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r6.claim: The passage quotes only the deluded humans because their corrupters are completely dumbstruck and unable to speak.
BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r6.anchor: ولعل الاقتصار على حكاية كلام الضالين للإيذان بأن المضلين قد أقحموا بالمرة

BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r1.claim: Mathwākum means your dwelling place, a place of settled residence.
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r1.anchor: أي : منزلكم فهو اسم مكان بمعنى مكان الإقامة

BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās divides creatures into angels destined wholly for Paradise, devils wholly for Hell, and humans and jinn who receive either reward or punishment.
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : الخلق أربعة : فخلق في الجنة كلهم

BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r3.speaker: صاحب التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r3.claim: The exception concerns people who repent and return to God in this life, so Hell will not be their abode; it does not apply to those eternally in Hell.
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r3.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : {إلا ما شاء الله}

BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r4.claim: One view takes mā as a verbal noun with an omitted genitive, and makes the exception modify the whole preceding statement about eternal residence.
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ما مصدرية بتقدير مضاف كما في آتيك خفوق النجم

BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r5.claim: On this view, the damned may be moved from the fire to a valley of freezing cold that tears their limbs apart; their cries to return to Hell make the exception ironic.
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r5.anchor: فقد روي أنهم ينقلون من عذاب النار ويدخلون واديا فيه من الزمهرير

BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r6.speaker: تفسير الجلالين
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r6.claim: Al-Jalālayn explains the exception as periods when they are taken out to drink boiling water, while outside the fire.

BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r7.claim: Another view says a door to Paradise opens before the damned; they rush toward it, but it closes as they arrive.
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r7.anchor: وقيل : يفتح لهم وهم في النار باب إلى الجنة فيسرعون نحوه

BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r8.claim: Another explanation places the exception before entry into Hell, during the delay before admission and eternal residence; outward scholars interpret the exception this way.
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r8.anchor: وقيل : {إلا ما شآء الله} قبل الدخول

BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r9.speaker: حضرة الشيخ نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r9.claim: Najm al-Dīn alludes to a subtle realization known to those who know God but beyond ordinary understanding, advising that it be disclosed only to spiritual wayfarers.
BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r9.anchor: إلا أن حضرة الشيخ نجم الدين قدس سره قال في ذلك : حفظا لظاهر الشرع

BURSEVI:v3p80#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p80#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p80#2/r1.claim: God's wisdom is evident, among other things, in consigning the devils' allies to Hell.
BURSEVI:v3p80#2/r1.anchor: {إن ربك حكيم} في أفعاله ومنها تخليد أولياء الشياطين في النار

BURSEVI:v3p80#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p80#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p80#2/r2.claim: God knows the states and deeds of both peoples and the recompense fitting for them.
BURSEVI:v3p80#2/r2.anchor: {عليم} بأحوال الثقلين وأعمالهم وبما يليق بها من الجزاء

DURR-FULL:v3p357/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the jinn greatly increased their number among humans by leading many of them astray.
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {قد استكثرتم من الإنس} يقول: في ضلالتكم إياهم يعني أضللتم منهم كثيرا

DURR-FULL:v3p357/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r2.claim: On the exception from eternal punishment, Ibn Abbas cautions that no one should decide on God's behalf whether His creatures enter Paradise or Hell.
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r2.anchor: وفي قوله {قال النار مثواكم خالدين فيها إلا ما شاء الله} قال: إن هذه الآية لا ينبغي لأحد أن يحكم على الله في خلقه

DURR-FULL:v3p357/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r3.claim: Al-Hasan understands the jinn's having greatly used mankind as their increasing the number of Hell's people on Judgment Day.
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r3.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الإنس} قال: استكثرتم ربكم أهل النار يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v3p357/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the mutual enjoyment consisted in the jinn commanding and humans carrying out their commands.
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r4.anchor: قال الحسن: وما كان استمتاع بعضهم ببعض إلا أن الجن أمرت وعملت الإنس

DURR-FULL:v3p357/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b glosses their mutual enjoyment as their companionship in worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r5.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب في قوله {ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض} قال: الصحابة في الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v3p357/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b identifies the appointed term they reached as death.
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب في قوله {ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض} قال: الصحابة في الدنيا {وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا} قال: الموت

DURR-FULL:v3p357/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says pre-Islamic men sought a valley's jinn chief's protection when settling there; this was the mutual benefit they cited at the Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r7.anchor: عن ابن أبي جريج في قوله {ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض} قال: كان الرجل في الجاهلية ينزل بالأرض فيقول: أعوذ بكبير هذا الوادي

DURR-FULL:v3p357/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj, like Muhammad ibn Ka'b, says the appointed term means death.
DURR-FULL:v3p357/r8.anchor: فذلك استمتاعهم فاعتذروا به يوم القيامة {وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا} قال: الموت

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r1.claim: He says the gathering is death.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد : ويوم نحشرهم جميعا قال : الحشر : الموت

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r2.claim: He says the jinn led many humans astray.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الانس في ضلالتكم اياهم ، يعني : اضللتم منهم كثيرا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r3.claim: He glosses the phrase as “many whom you led astray.”
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد ، في قوله : قد استكثرتم من الانس : كثر من اغويتم

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r4.claim: He says the jinn led many humans astray.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة ، في قوله : يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الانس قال : اضللتم كثيرا من الانس

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r5.claim: He says the Lord made the people of Hell numerous on the Day of Resurrection.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r5.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الانس قال : استكثر ربكم اهل النار يوم القيامة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r6.claim: He says the mutual enjoyment consisted of the jinn commanding and humans acting.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r6.anchor: قال الحسن : وما كان استمتاع بعضهم ببعض الا ان الجن امرت وعملت الانس

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r7.claim: He glosses the mutual enjoyment as the companions' worldly association.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r7.anchor: قال : سمعت محمد بن كعب يقول في قوله : ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض قال : الصحابة في الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r8.claim: He repeats that the jinn commanded and the humans acted.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r8.anchor: عن الحسن ، في قوله : وبلغنا اجلنا الذي اجلت لنا ، قال : امرت الجن ، وعملت الانس

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r9.claim: He glosses the appointed term as death; al-Sadi is reported to give the same gloss.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r9.anchor: قال : سمعت محمد بن كعب يقول في قوله : وبلغنا اجلنا الذي اجلت لنا قال : الموت

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r10.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r10.claim: He is also reported to gloss the appointed term as death.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r10.anchor: وروى عن السدي انه قال : الموت

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r11.claim: He says no one should pronounce judgment for God about His creatures by assigning them to Paradise or Hell.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1387#2/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : قال النار مثواكم خالدين فيها الا ما شاء الله ان ربك حكيم عليم قال : ان هذه الاية لا ينبغي لاحد ان يحكم على الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r1.claim: Yawm is governed by implied udhkur or possibly the preceding wali, coordinated with the syntactic position of 6:127's ‘because of what they did.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r1.anchor: يوم نصب بفعل مضمر تقديره واذكر يوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r2.claim: The pronoun includes both jinn and human groups, unbelievers under defilement and those granted the Abode of Peace; ‘all together’ confirms the scope.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r2.anchor: والضمير في يحشرهم عائد على الطائفتين الذين يجعل الله الرجس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r3.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r3.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads with yāʾ, others with nūn; both are valid.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r4.claim: An implied verb before ‘O company of jinn’ is estimated as ‘We say.’ Al-ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Qatāda say the jinn excessively misled humans.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r4.anchor: وفي الكلام فعل مضمر يدل عليه ظاهر الكلام تقديره نقول يا معشر الجن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r5.claim: Human allies speak in excuse, saying both sides benefited. Al-Ṭabarī recounts Arabs seeking a valley jinn's protection; they credited safety to the jinn. Other worldly forms of benefit are possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r5.anchor: وقال الكفار من الإنس وهم أولياء الجن الموبخين على جهة الاعتذار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says the appointed term is death; other views say Resurrection or the limit of mutual enjoyment, acknowledging God's decree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r6.anchor: قال السدي هو الموت الذي انتهى الكل منهم إليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r7.claim: God's report follows their plea; past tense reports certain future action, common and eloquent Qurʾānic usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: قال النار مثواكم الآية، إخبار من الله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r8.speaker: الزجاج وأبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes mathwā as place of recompense or abode. Abu ʿAlī takes it as verbal noun because it governs khalidīn, estimating ‘the Fire is the possessor of your abode.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r8.anchor: ومثواكم أي موضع ثوابكم كمقامكم الذي هو موضع الإقامة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r9.claim: One group takes mā as man, exempting those who believe in worldly life after unbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345/r9.anchor: قالت فرقة ما بمعنى من، فالمراد إلا من شاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345#2/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says illā means ‘other than’ and the exception is added punishment God wills; al-Zajjāj inclines to this. Al-Ṭabarī takes it as the interval before entry into Fire, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the wording permits.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345#2/r1.anchor: وقال الفراء إلا بمعنى سوى، والمراد سوى ما يشاء من زيادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345#2/r2.speaker: الطبري عن ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345#2/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports Ibn ʿAbbās said the exception is their final state known to God and no one should judge whether God puts a person in Paradise or Fire; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this as unsound against consensus of eternal punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345#2/r2.anchor: وقال الطبري عن ابن عباس انه كان يتناول في هذا الاستثناء أنه مبلغ حال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the exception as an address to the Prophet and community, exempting unbelievers whom God knows will later believe; mā can denote rational persons, and Wise/Knowing fits this knowledge and just punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p345#2/r3.anchor: ويتجه عندي في هذا الاستثناء أن يكون مخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r1.claim: The gathering includes both jinn and humans.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r1.anchor: يعني الجن والإنس وقرأ حفص عن عاصم يحشرهم بالياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r2.claim: Hafs transmits from ʿAsim the reading yaḥshuruhum with yaʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r2.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم يحشرهم بالياء قال أبو سليمان يعني المشركين وشياطينهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r3.speaker: أبو سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r3.claim: Abu Sulayman says the referents are polytheists and their devils, who prompted arguments against what God forbade of carrion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r3.anchor: قال أبو سليمان يعني المشركين وشياطينهم الذين كانوا يوحون إليهم بالمجادلة لكم فيما حرمه الله من الميتة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r4.claim: The wording has an ellipsis: it is as though they are told, O assembly; maʿshar is a group united in one matter, with plural maʿashir.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r4.anchor: فيه إضمار فيقال لهم يا معشر والمعشر الجماعة أمرهم واحد والجمع المعاشر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r5.claim: The jinn amassed many humans by misleading and leading them astray.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r5.anchor: ﴿ قد استكثرتم من الإنس ﴾ أي من إغوائهم وإضلالهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r6.claim: The human allies are those whom the jinn led astray.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r6.anchor: ﴿ وقال أولياؤهم من الإنس ﴾ يعني الذين أضلهم الجن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r7.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس، مقاتل، الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r7.claim: One view says humans sought refuge with the chief of a valley when camping; jinn enjoyed humans' dependence and boasted that they had mastered them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r7.anchor: أنهم كانوا إذا سافروا فنزلوا واديا وأرادوا مبيتا قال أحدهم أعوذ بعظيم هذا الوادي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r8.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس، محمد بن كعب، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r8.claim: Another view says jinn enjoyed humans' obedience to their invitations into error, disbelief, and sin; humans enjoyed the jinn's beautifying and making their desires easy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r8.anchor: والثاني أن استمتاع الجن بالإنس طاعتهم لهم فيما يغرونهم به من الضلالة والكفر والمعاصي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r9.claim: A third view says jinn enjoyed seducing humans, while humans enjoyed receiving magic, soothsaying, and similar practices.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r9.anchor: والثالث أن استمتاع الجن بالإنس إغواؤهم إياهم واستمتاع الإنس بالجن ما يتلقون منهم من السحر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r10.claim: The jinn meant here are devils.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p123/r10.anchor: والمراد بالجن في هذه الآية الشياطين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r1.speaker: الحسن، السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r1.claim: One view says the appointed term they reached was death.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r2.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r2.claim: A second view says the appointed term was the Resurrection.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines mathwa as a dwelling or place of residence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج المثوى المقام وخالدين منصوب على الحال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r4.claim: Khalidin is accusative as a circumstantial expression; the meaning is that the Fire is their abode in a state of everlasting residence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r4.anchor: وخالدين منصوب على الحال المعنى النار مقامكم في حال خلود دائم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r5.claim: One explanation treats the exception as covering the time from the Resurrection until their emergence from graves and their period of accounting; they then remain eternally in the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r5.anchor: هو استثناء من يوم القيامة والمعنى ﴿ خالدين فيها ﴾ مذ يبعثون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r6.claim: Another possible explanation is that God may increase their punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ﴿ إلا ما شاء الله ﴾ أن يزيدهم من العذاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r7.claim: A further reported view excludes the time they spent in this world before punishment began; Ibn al-Jawzi refers readers to the fuller discussion in Hud.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p124/r7.anchor: وقيل في هذا غير قول ستجدها مشروحة في هود إن شاء الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r1.claim: God tells Muhammad to recall this gathering while recounting and warning; the gathered humans are the jinn’s allies who worshipped, sought refuge in, and obeyed them, as they mutually inspired deceptive speech.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r2.claim: The jinn greatly increased their share of humanity by misleading and seducing many, as in the warning that Satan led many people astray.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى قوله: {قد استكثرتم من الإنس} أي: من إضلالهم وإغوائهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Qatada likewise explain that the jinn misled many humans.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r3.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الإنس} يعني: أضللتم منهم كثيرا. وكذلك قال مجاهد، والحسن، وقتادة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r1.claim: The humans who allied themselves with the jinn respond to God with this explanation of their mutual enjoyment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r1.anchor: يعني: أن أولياء الجن من الإنس قالوا مجيبين لله تعالى عن ذلك بهذا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the jinn commanded people and the humans carried out their commands; that was the mutual enjoyment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: وما كان استمتاع بعضهم ببعض إلا أن الجن أمرت، وعملت الإنس.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb glosses their mutual enjoyment as the companions’ enjoyment of one another in worldly life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r3.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب في قوله: {ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض} قال: الصحابة في الدنيا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj describes a pre-Islamic man seeking refuge with the chief of a valley; this was the mutual benefit they now cite as an excuse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r4.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: كان الرجل في الجاهلية ينزل الأرض، فيقول:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r5.claim: Jinn benefited when humans revered and called on them for help; they boasted that they had gained mastery over humans and jinn.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r5.anchor: ما ينال الجن من الإنس من تعظيمهم إياهم في استعانتهم بهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the appointed term they reached is death.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r1.anchor: وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا} قال السدي، أي الموت.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r2.claim: The fire is the abode and dwelling of the jinn and their human allies, where they remain eternally, subject to God’s will.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r3.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r3.claim: Some say the exception to eternal punishment refers to the period in the barzakh.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم: يرجع معنى [هذا] (1) الاستثناء إلى البرزخ.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r4.claim: Others say the exception refers to the duration of worldly life; Ibn Kathir postpones fuller treatment of these and other views to 11:107.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هذا رد إلى مدة الدنيا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says this verse forbids anyone from deciding for God about His creatures by assigning them to Paradise or Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r5.anchor: إن هذه الآية آية لا ينبغي لأحد أن يحكم على الله في خلقه، ولا ينزلهم جنة ولا نارا.

JISHUMI:v3p2404/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r2.claim: Istimtāʿ means benefiting from something; matāʿ is anything one uses or gains benefit from.
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r2.anchor: والاستمتاع بالشيء: الانتفاع به، يقال: استمتعت به؛ أي: انتفعت

JISHUMI:v3p2404/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r3.claim: Mutʿat al-ṭalāq is a benefit given to a divorced woman when no dowry was fixed and no intercourse occurred; she receives the gift but no mahr.
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r3.anchor: وهو للمطلقة من غير فرض ولا مسيس، فتعطى المتعة، ولا مهر لها

JISHUMI:v3p2404/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r4.claim: Mutʿat al-ḥajj means performing ʿumra in the pilgrimage months, leaving consecration, staying in Mecca, then performing ḥajj that year.
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r4.anchor: ومتعة الحج: وهو أن يأتي بالعمرة في أشهر الحج، ثم يحل ويقيم بمكة ثم يحج من سنته

JISHUMI:v3p2404/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r5.claim: Mutʿat al-nikāḥ is temporary marriage, which jurists deem abrogated and forbidden; this is also al-Hādī's position.
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r5.anchor: ومتعة النكاح: وهو النكاح الموقت، وهو منسوخ حرام عند الفقهاء، وهو مذهب الهادي

JISHUMI:v3p2404/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r6.speaker: عمر
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r6.claim: The source cites ʿUmar saying that two forms of mutʿa existed in the Prophet's time and that he would prohibit and punish them: pilgrimage and marriage.
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r6.anchor: فأما قول عمر: (متعتان كانتا على عهد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنا أنهى عنهما وأعاقب عليهما

JISHUMI:v3p2404/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r7.claim: The source understands ʿUmar's pilgrimage mutʿa as dissolving iḥrām; the Prophet permitted this to his Companions and it was later abrogated.
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r7.anchor: فالمراد ما ذكرنا، ومتعة الحج: هو فسخ الإحرام، وكان أذن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لأصحابه في ذلك، ثم نسخ

JISHUMI:v3p2404/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r8.claim: Amtaʿtu bi-mālī means the same as tamattaʿtu; amtaʿtu ʿan someone means I became independent of them.
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r8.anchor: وأمتعت بمالي مثل تمتعت، ويقال: أمتعت عن فلان: استغنيت عنه

JISHUMI:v3p2404/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r9.claim: The word is also used in 4:24, 'whatever benefit you have taken from them,' and in references to the temporary benefits of worldly life.
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r9.anchor: ومنه: (فما استمتعتم به منهن) ومتاع الحياة الدنيا: منافعها التي لا تدوم

JISHUMI:v3p2404/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r10.claim: Ajal is the duration of a thing; ājil is the opposite of immediate or present.
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r10.anchor: والأجل: مدة الشيء، والآجل: ضد العاجل

JISHUMI:v3p2404/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r11.claim: Mathwā means a place of residence, from thawā, to stay or dwell; athwā has the same sense.
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r11.anchor: والمثوى: المقام، يقال: ثوى يثوي ثواء، قال الشاعر

JISHUMI:v3p2404/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r12.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r12.claim: A poet's line about a year spent dwelling there is cited as evidence for the sense of residence.
JISHUMI:v3p2404/r12.anchor: قال الشاعر: لقد كان في حول ثواء ثويته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r1.claim: The temporal phrase is governed by an omitted verb (‘remember the day’), or attached to the statement that they worshipped jinn, or to the gathering and address itself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r1.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف ، أي واذكر يوم نحشرهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r2.claim: The pronoun includes all gathered beings from humans, jinn, and others.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r2.anchor: والضمير لمن يحشر من الثقلين وغيرهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r3.claim: The jinn addressed here are devils.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r3.anchor: والجن هم الشياطين { قد استكثرتم من الإنس } أضللتم منهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r4.claim: The devils led many humans astray or made many of them their followers, like a commander amassing soldiers or a man collecting partisans.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r4.anchor: أضللتم منهم كثيرا أو جعلتموهم أتباعكم فحشر معكم منهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r5.claim: The human allies are those who obeyed the jinn and listened to their whispering.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r6.claim: Humans benefited from devils’ guidance to desires and ways to reach them; devils benefited from human obedience that assisted their seduction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r6.anchor: أي انتفع الإنس بالشياطين حيث دلوهم على الشهوات وعلى أسباب التوصل إليها ، وانتفع الجن بالإنس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r7.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r7.claim: Another explanation links human enjoyment of jinn to seeking their protection when entering a valley, as in 72:6; jinn enjoyed humans’ belief in their power to protect.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r7.anchor: وقيل : استمتاع الإنس بالجن ما في قوله : { وأنه كان رجال من الإنس يعوذون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r8.claim: In that explanation, jinn benefited from humans’ acknowledgment that they could protect them and grant them refuge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r8.anchor: واستمتاع الجن والإنس : اعتراف الإنس لهم بأنهم يقدرون على الدفع عنه إجارتهم لهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r9.claim: The human allies mean the Day of Resurrection and confess their obedience to devils, pursuit of desire, denial of resurrection, submission to God, and regret.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r9.anchor: وهذا الكلام اعتراف بما كان منهم من طاعة الشياطين واتباع الهوى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r10.claim: An unassigned report says the damned may be moved from fire to the torment of freezing cold, where their limbs separate and they cry to be returned to Hell.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r10.anchor: فقد روي أنهم يدخلون واديا فيه من الزمهرير و يميز بعض أوصالهم من بعض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r11.claim: Alternatively, the exception is a tormenting threat: an avenger appears to offer relief only when he means to intensify punishment, ironically suggesting reprieve.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r11.anchor: فيكون قوله : إلا إذا شئت ، من أشد الوعيد ، مع تهكم بالموعد لخروجه في صورة الاستثناء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r12.claim: God acts only according to wisdom and knows that unbelievers deserve everlasting punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p61/r12.anchor: لا يفعل شيئا إلا بموجب الحكمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r1.claim: The verse means that God will gather all the jinn and humans together on the Day of Resurrection.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r1.anchor: يعني يحشر الجن والإنس جميعا يوم القيامة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، قتادة، مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r2.claim: These authorities take the address to mean that the jinn led many humans astray.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r2.anchor: قد استكثرتم من إغوئهم وإضلالهم , قاله ابن عباس , والحسن , وقتادة , ومجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r3.claim: Another interpretation says the jinn amassed many human followers through their misleading.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r3.anchor: والثاني قد استكثرتم من الإنس بإغوائكم لهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r4.claim: One interpretation says humans and jinn enjoyed one another's companionship through mutual aid and support.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r4.anchor: معناه استمتع بعضنا بصحبة بعض في التعاون والتعاضد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r5.claim: A second interpretation says they enjoyed one another through the pursuit of desires and sins that each made attractive.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r5.anchor: استمتع بعضنا ببعض فيما زينوه من اتباع الأهواء وارتكاب المعاصي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r6.speaker: الحسن، ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r6.claim: Hasan and Ibn Jurayj say the humans' enjoyment of jinn was seeking refuge in them, as in 72:6.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r6.anchor: أن الاستمتاع بهم ما كانوا عليه من التعوذ بهم كقوله تعالى :

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r7.claim: On that interpretation, the enjoyment may be humans' use of jinn or humans' enjoyment of one another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r7.anchor: أحدهما : أنه استمتاع الإنس بالجن . والثاني : أنه استمتاع الإنس بعضهم ببعض .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r8.claim: A further view says humans believed jinn could benefit them, while jinn believed humans could benefit them in return.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r8.anchor: أن الإنس استمتعوا بالجن , والجن استمتعوا بالإنس في اعتقادهم أنهم يقدرون على النفع .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r9.speaker: الحسن، السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r9.claim: Hasan and al-Suddi say the appointed term they reached is death.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r10.claim: Another interpretation identifies the appointed term as the Resurrection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r11.claim: Mathwa means the dwelling or place of residence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r11.anchor: أي منزل إقامتكم , لأن المثوى الإقامة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r12.claim: A line of poetry is cited as evidence for the word thawa, to stay or reside.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p168/r12.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر : لقد كان في حول ثواء ثويته

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r1.speaker: سيبويه
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r1.claim: Sibawayh takes illa here as meaning 'but,' a corrective exception.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r2.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r2.claim: Al-Farra takes illa to mean 'other than' or 'besides.'

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r3.speaker: الجمهور
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r3.claim: The majority take the exception in its ordinary, literal sense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r3.anchor: أنها مستعملة على حقيقتها , وهو قول الجمهور .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r4.claim: One interpretation limits the exception to the interval from resurrection until the gathered people enter Hell, when they are not yet in the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r4.anchor: وذلك ما بين بعثهم من قبورهم إلى حين مصيرهم إلى جهنم , فكأنه قال : النار مثواكم خالدين فيها إلا هذه المدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r5.claim: Another interpretation makes the exception concern the manner of punishment, not eternal residence in Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r5.anchor: من تجديد جلودهم بعد إحراقها وتصريفهم في أنواع العذاب أو تركهم فيها على حالتهم الأولى , فيكون الاستثناء في صفة العذاب لا في الخلود في النار .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the amount and duration of punishment are left to God's will; no one should pronounce on God's creatures or assign them to Paradise or Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p169/r6.anchor: أنه جعل أمرهم في مبلغ عذابهم ومدته إلى مشيئته تعالى , قاله ابن عباس , قال : ولا ينبغي لأحد أن يحكم على الله في خلقه

MUQATIL:6:128/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:128/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:128/r1.claim: The gathering includes disbelieving humans, devils, and jinn; the words mean that God gathers them all.
MUQATIL:6:128/r1.anchor: { ويوم يحشرهم } ، يعنى كفار الإنس والشياطين والجن، يقول: ويوم نجمعهم،

MUQATIL:6:128/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:128/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:128/r2.claim: God's address to the company of jinn is directed to the devils.
MUQATIL:6:128/r2.anchor: { جميعا يامعشر الجن } ، ثم يقول للشياطين: { قد استكثرتم من الإنس }

MUQATIL:6:128/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:128/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:128/r3.claim: The devils amassed many humans by leading them astray; the human disbelievers had allied with and sought protection from the jinn.
MUQATIL:6:128/r3.anchor: { قد استكثرتم من الإنس } ، يعنى من ضلال الإنس فيما أضللتم منهم، وذلك أن كفار الإنس كانوا تولوا الجن وأعاذوا بهم،

MUQATIL:6:128/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:128/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:128/r4.claim: A traveler afraid at night in the desert would seek the valley's jinn chief's protection; the jinn considered human appeals a source of honor.
MUQATIL:6:128/r4.anchor: { ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض } ، كاستمتاع الإنس بالجن، وذلك أن الرجل كان إذا سافر فأدركه الليل بأرض القفر خاف،

MUQATIL:6:128/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:128/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:128/r5.claim: The jinn said humans had made them eminent when they sought their protection, increasing the jinn's honor.
MUQATIL:6:128/r5.anchor: وكان استمتاع الجن بالإنس أن يقولوا: لقد سودتنا الإنس حين فزعوا إلينا، فيزدادوا بذلك شرفا،

MUQATIL:6:128/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:128/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:128/r6.claim: Their appointed term is their death in this world.
MUQATIL:6:128/r6.anchor: { وبلغنآ أجلنا } الموت { الذي أجلت لنا } فى الدنيا،

MUQATIL:6:128/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:128/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:128/r7.claim: The fire is the dwelling place of the disbelievers, where they remain forever.
MUQATIL:6:128/r7.anchor: { قال النار مثواكم } ، ومثوى الكافرين، { خالدين فيها } أبدا،

MUQATIL:6:128/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:128/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:128/r8.claim: The exception refers to people of God's oneness: they will not remain eternally in Hell.
MUQATIL:6:128/r8.anchor: { إلا ما شاء الله } ، واستثنى أهل التوحيد، أنهم لا يخلدون فيها،

MUQATIL:6:128/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:128/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:128/r9.claim: God is wise in decreeing the fire for those who disobey Him, and knows those who do not disobey Him.
MUQATIL:6:128/r9.anchor: { إن ربك حكيم } ، يعنى حكم النار لمن عصاه، { عليم } [آية: 128]، يقول: عالم بمن لا يعصيه.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r1.speaker: حفص
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ reads the verb with yāʾ: yaḥshuruhum.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r1.anchor: وبالياء حفص أى واذكر يوم نحشرهم أو ويوم نحشرهم قلنا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r2.claim: The phrase may be completed as remember the day We gather them, or as on the day We gather them, We said.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r2.anchor: أى واذكر يوم نحشرهم أو ويوم نحشرهم قلنا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r3.claim: The jinn misled many humans and made them their followers, like an emir who amassed many troops.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r3.anchor: أضللتم منهم كثيرا وجعلتموهم أتباعكم كما تقول استكثر الأمير من الجنود

NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r4.claim: The human allies are those who obeyed the jinn and listened to their whispers.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r5.claim: Humans benefited from demons' guidance to desires and their means; demons benefited from humans' obedience and help in seduction.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r5.anchor: انتفع الإنس بالشياطين حيث دلوهم على الشهوات وعلى أسباب التوصل إليها وانتفع الجن بالإنس

NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r6.claim: They mean the resurrection day; their words confess obedience to Satan, following desire, and denial of resurrection, and express regret.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r6.anchor: يعنون يوم البعث وهذا الكلام اعتراف بما كان منهم من طاعة الشياطين واتباع الهوى والتكذيب بالبعث وتحسر على حالهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r7.claim: Khālidīn is a circumstantial accusative governed by the meaning of the possessive construction; mathwā cannot govern it because a place does not govern anything.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r7.anchor: ﴿ خالدين فيها ﴾ حال والعامل معنى الإضافة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r8.claim: They abide in the Fire forever except during periods when they are moved from scorching fire to the torment of extreme cold.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r8.anchor: إلا الأوقات التى ينقلون فيها من عذاب السعير إلى عذاب الزمهرير

NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r9.claim: God is wise in what He does to allies and enemies, and knows their deeds so He repays each accordingly.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p345#2/r9.anchor: ﴿ إن ربك حكيم ﴾ فيما يفعل بأوليائه وأعدائه ﴿ عليم ﴾ بأعمالهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r1.claim: Yawma is accusative under an omitted verb, understood as: the day We gather them, We will say this.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r1.anchor: نصب على الفعل المحذوف، أي ويوم نحشرهم نقول.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r2.claim: Jamiʿan is an accusative circumstantial expression, referring to the gathering of all creation at the Resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r2.anchor: جميعا } نصب على الحال. والمراد حشر جميع الخلق

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r3.claim: Maʿshar al-jinn is a vocative construction in genitive annexation.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r3.anchor: يامعشر الجن } نداء مضاف. { قد استكثرتم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r4.claim: The phrase means taking much enjoyment from humans, with an annexed verbal noun and its object elided; the following mutual-enjoyment phrase supports this syntax.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r4.anchor: أي من الاستمتاع بالإنس فحذف المصدر المضاف إلى المفعول، وحرف الجر يدل على ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects the view that only jinn benefited from humans because humans accepted their influence; he says each side enjoyed the other.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r5.anchor: وهذا يرد قول من قال: إن الجن هم الذين استمتعوا من الإنس لأن الإنس قبلوا منهم. والصحيح أن كل واحد مستمتع بصاحبه.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r6.claim: Jinn enjoyed human obedience, while humans enjoyed accepting their inducements to fornication and wine drinking.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r6.anchor: والتقدير في العربية: استمتع بعضنا بعضا فاستمتاع الجن من الإنس أنهم تلذذوا بطاعة الإنس إياهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r7.claim: One account says travelers who feared a valley sought refuge with its jinn; this is linked to the Qur'anic report about humans seeking refuge with jinn.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r7.anchor: وقيل: كان الرجل إذا مر بواد في سفره وخاف على نفسه قال: أعوذ برب هذا الوادي

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r8.claim: In that account, humans benefited from jinn protection, while jinn benefited humans through frightening rumors, soothsaying, and sorcery.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r8.anchor: فهذا استمتاع الإنس بالجن. وأما استمتاع الجن بالإنس فما كانوا يلقون إليهم من الأراجيف والكهانة والسحر.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r9.claim: Another view says jinn benefited from humans because humans acknowledged that jinn could protect them from what they feared.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r9.anchor: وقيل: استمتاع الجن بالأنس أنهم يعترفون أن الجن يقدرون أن يدفعوا عنهم ما يحذرون.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r10.claim: The exchange is a public reproach of those who strayed and those who led others astray, before all creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r10.anchor: ومعنى الآية تقريع الضالين والمضلين وتوبيخهم في الآخرة على أعين العالمين.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r11.claim: Their appointed term means death and the grave, and they arrive regretting their choices.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r12.claim: Mathwa means the place of dwelling or staying.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r13.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj treats the exception as disconnected and referring to the Resurrection: the time from rising from graves through the reckoning is excluded from their being in Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r13.anchor: قال الزجاج: يرجع إلى يوم القيامة، أي خالدين في النار

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r14.claim: Another view makes the exception refer to Hell, excluding any periods in which God wills to punish them by something other than fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r14.anchor: وقيل: يرجع الاستثناء إلى النار، أي إلا ما شاء الله من تعذيبكم بغير النار

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas says the exception is for believers, with ma understood to mean man.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r15.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الاستثناء لأهل الإيمان.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas also says the verse requires suspending judgment about all unbelievers; al-Qurtubi explains this as those still alive, who might yet accept Islam.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r16.anchor: وعنه أيضا أنه قال: هذه الآية توجب الوقف في جميع الكفار. ومعنى ذلك أنها توجب الوقف فيمن لم يمت، إذ قد يسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r17.claim: Another explanation excludes their time in worldly life, when they were not yet being punished.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r17.anchor: وقيل: «إلا ما شاء الله» من كونهم في الدنيا بغير عذاب.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r18.claim: Al-Qurtubi says this verse has the same meaning as the passage in Hud about the wretched being in the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128/r18.anchor: ومعنى هذه الآية معنى الآية التي في «هود». قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:6:128#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128#2/r1.claim: God is wise in punishing them and in all His acts, and knows the measure of their requital.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:128#2/r1.anchor: أي في عقوبتهم وفي جميع أفعاله { عليم } بمقدار مجازاتهم

QASHANI:6:126-128/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:126-128/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:126-128/r6.claim: The day of gathering is the day of absolute unitive gathering, when the jinn are the powers of the lower self.
QASHANI:6:126-128/r6.anchor: قلنا { يا معشر } جن القوى النفسانية

QASHANI:6:126-128/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:126-128/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:126-128/r7.claim: The humans whom the psychic powers amassed may be the outer senses and limbs, which they induce to obey through worldly trinkets, physical pleasures, and sinful whisperings.
QASHANI:6:126-128/r7.anchor: من الحواس والأعضاء الظاهرة أو من

QASHANI:6:126-128/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:126-128/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:126-128/r8.claim: Alternatively, the amassed humans are human forms that the psychic powers make their followers through seductive worldly goods and bodily delights.

QASHANI:6:126-128/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:126-128/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:126-128/r9.claim: The mutual enjoyment is each side benefiting from the other within their collective form.
QASHANI:6:126-128/r9.anchor: بانتفاع كل منا في صورة الجمعية بالآخر

QASHANI:6:126-128/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:126-128/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:126-128/r10.claim: Their appointed term may be death or bodily resurrection in the ugliest form and most wretched life.
QASHANI:6:126-128/r10.anchor: بالموت أو بالمعاد الجسماني على أقبح الصور وأسوأ العيش

QASHANI:6:126-128/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:126-128/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:126-128/r11.claim: The fire is deprivation from pleasures and the experience of pain; the exception may mean a respite or the rescue of those whose belief in shirk was not firmly rooted.
QASHANI:6:126-128/r11.anchor: نار الحرمان عن اللذات ووجدان الآلام

QASHANI:6:126-128/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:126-128/r12.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:126-128/r12.claim: God’s wisdom punishes according to acquired soul-dispositions; His knowledge distinguishes those punished endlessly for belief from those punished temporarily for evil deeds and then released.
QASHANI:6:126-128/r12.anchor: لا يعذبكم إلا بهيآت نفوسكم التي كسبتم

RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r1.claim: After describing those who follow the straight path, God sets the people of the Garden against the people of the Fire, placing warning after promise.
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r1.anchor: حال من يتمسك بالصراط المستقيم ، بين بعده حال من يكون بالضد

RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r2.speaker: author
