RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r2.claim: The accusative يوم depends on an omitted verb: remember the day; or it belongs with We gather and say; or We gather and say are coordinated; the event is too terrible to describe.
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r2.anchor: { ويوم يحشرهم } منصوب بمحذوف ، أي واذكر يوم

RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r3.claim: One view takes the pronoun as all morally responsible beings whom God will resurrect, though they were not mentioned immediately before.
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r3.anchor: يعودإلى المعلوم ، لا إلى المذكور ، وهو الثقلان

RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r4.claim: A second view takes the pronoun as the devils mentioned at 6:112.
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r4.anchor: في قوله : { وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبى عدوا شياطين الإنس والجن يوحى بعضهم إلى بعض

RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r5.claim: An omitted phrase means We gather them, then God says O company of jinn; His speech after the gathering rebukes them and makes them admit guilt after worldly defiance.
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r5.anchor: في الآية محذوف والتقدير : يوم نحشرهم جميعا فنقول : يا معشر الجن

RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r6.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj instead supplies a passive it is said to them, since he considers direct divine speech to unbelievers unlikely in light of 2:174.
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج : التقدير فيقال لهم يا معشر الجن ، لأنه يبعد

RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r7.claim: Jinn cannot literally multiply human beings, since only God creates bodies and life; the phrase means they called many humans toward misguidance and found them receptive.
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r7.anchor: هذا لا بد فيه من التأويل . لأن الجن لا يقدرون على الاستكثار

RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r8.claim: The text also implicitly rebukes the human allies: jinn invited them, humans accepted, and both shared in the wrongdoing; the verse then reports the humans' answer.
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r8.anchor: فكما قال للجن تبكيتا ، فكذلك قال للإنس توبيخا

RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r9.claim: The human allies describe themselves as absorbed in worldly benefits and pleasures until they reached this point and became certain of their bad end.
RAZI-FULL:v13p156/r9.anchor: فوصفوا أنفسهم بالتوفر على منافع الدنيا ، والاستمتاع بلذاتها

RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r1.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة والكلبي وابن جريج
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r1.claim: Al-Hasan, Ikrima, al-Kalbi and Ibn Jurayj say humans sought a jinn valley-master's protection while traveling, and jinn enjoyed being revered and boasting of their mastery; this is linked to 72:6.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r1.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن وعكرمة والكلبي وابن جريج واحتجوا على صحته بقوله تعالى : { وأنه كان رجال

RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers that humans obeyed jinn as leaders, benefiting them through service, while jinn drew humans toward desires and pleasures; this better explains jinn's many human followers than the rare valley-protection custom.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r2.anchor: وهذا القول اختيار الزجاج . قال : وهذا أولى من الوجه المتقدم

RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r3.claim: A second overall interpretation takes the statement as humans enjoying one another, since mutual enjoyment between humans is common and the speakers are human allies of jinn.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r3.anchor: هو كلام الإنس خاصة ، لأن استمتاع الجن بالإنس وبالعكس أمر قليل

RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r4.claim: They say their mutual enjoyment lasted until its fixed endpoint, after which failure, regret and remorse arrived too late.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r4.anchor: فالمعنى : أن ذلك الاستمتاع كان حاصلا إلى أجل معين ووقت محدود ،

RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r5.claim: One view identifies the appointed term as death; its proponents say the verse shows that every person, murdered or not, dies at an appointed time.

RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r6.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r6.claim: Another view identifies the appointed term as the time of release and empowerment.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون : هو وقت التخلية والتمكين

RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r7.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r7.claim: A third view identifies the appointed term as the time of reckoning on the Resurrection Day.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157/r7.anchor: وقال قوم : المراد وقت المحاسبة في القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r1.claim: Al-mathwā means the place of residence, abode, or final destination.

RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r2.claim: Although an ordinary abode can be left by death, God specifies that this abode is everlasting.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r2.anchor: فبين تعالى أن ذلك المقام والمثوى مخلد مؤبد وهو قوله : { خالدين فيها } .

RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r3.claim: One proposed exception is the intervals of reckoning, when they are not yet in the Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r3.anchor: المراد منه استثناء أوقات المحاسبة ، لأن في تلك الأحوال ليسوا بخالدين في النار :

RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r4.claim: A report says they are moved from the Fire to a valley of intense cold, then plead to return to Hellfire's heat.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r4.anchor: وروي أنهم يدخلون واديا فيه برد شديد فهم يطلبون الرد من ذلك البرد إلى حر الجحيم .

RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the exception to mean people foreknown by God to become Muslims and believe the Prophet; mā here means man.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس : استثنى الله تعالى قوما سبق في علمه أنهم يسلمون ويصدقون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم .

RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj prefers the reckoning-period interpretation because the exception concerns the Resurrection day named in the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج : والقول الأول أولى . لأن معنى الاستثناء إنما هو من يوم القيامة ، لأن قوله :

RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r7.claim: They remain from resurrection; the exception is the time spent emerging from their graves and being reckoned.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r7.anchor: ثم قال تعالى : { خالدين فيها } منذ يبعثون { إلا ما شاء الله } من مقدار حشرهم من قبورهم

RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r8.claim: Abū Muslim says the exception modifies their appointed lifespan: some were destroyed before the term they would have reached had they believed.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r8.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : هذا الاستثناء غير راجع إلى الخلود ، وإنما هو راجع إلى الأجل المؤجل لهم

RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r9.claim: Abū Muslim's reading is illustrated by earlier peoples destroyed before their appointed term, including Noah's, ʿĀd's, and Thamūd's peoples.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r9.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { ألم يروا كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من قرن } ( الأنعام : 6 )

RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r10.claim: The Abū Muslim interpretation is possible, but al-Rāzī rejects it because it departs from the verse's word order when the apparent reading works.
RAZI-FULL:v13p157#2/r10.anchor: واعلم أن هذا الوجه وإن كان محتملا إلا أنه ترك لظاهر ترتيب ألفاظ هذه الآية .

STUDYQURAN:6:128/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r1.claim: The jinn are addressed directly; they had led many people astray through flowery discourse or whispering.
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r1.anchor: many among mankind have you claimed refers to the many people the jinn led astray through flowery discourse

STUDYQURAN:6:128/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r2.claim: “Claimed” does not mean that jinn possessed people and controlled their wills; they called or tempted people, who responded.
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r2.anchor: the jinn “possessed” these human beings in the sense of controlling their will, but rather that the jinn merely called or tempted them toward wrongdoing, and that many responded

STUDYQURAN:6:128/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r3.claim: One interpretation takes the appointed term as the onset of the Day of Judgment.
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r3.anchor: may refer to the onset of the Day of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:6:128/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the appointed term as the end of earthly lives.
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r4.anchor: or simply to the end of their earthly lives

STUDYQURAN:6:128/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r5.claim: People profited from false assurances when they called on jinn for protection from harm.
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r5.anchor: human beings profited from the false assurances they received by calling upon the jinn for protection against harm

STUDYQURAN:6:128/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r6.claim: Jinn profited because people attributed to them greatness, power, and authority they did not possess.
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r6.anchor: the jinn profited from this arrangement insofar as it attributed to them a greatness, power, and authority they did not actually possess

STUDYQURAN:6:128/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r7.claim: The word for abode here is mathwā, whereas verse 127 uses dār.
STUDYQURAN:6:128/r7.anchor: the Fire is to be their abode (here mathwā, instead of dār, as in v. 127)

TABATABAI:6:128/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128/r1.claim: These verses continue the preceding discussion by explaining how God makes some wrongdoers guardians over others, such as Satans over unbelievers, without injustice: on Judgment Day they will admit their shirk and sins followed their own choice after warning.
TABATABAI:6:128/r1.anchor: بيان الآيات متصلة بما قبلها وهي تفسر معنى ولاية بعض الظالمين بعضا المجعولة من الله

TABATABAI:6:128/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128/r2.claim: Divine decree does not remove the choice on which accountability rests, and human choice does not conflict with decree: God decrees their chosen following of Satan rather than compelling it.
TABATABAI:6:128/r2.anchor: فالقضاء الإلهي لا يسلب عنهم الاختيار الذي عليه مدار المؤاخذة والمجازاة

TABATABAI:6:128/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128/r3.claim: God has no need of anything they possess that could justify oppression; He created them in mercy and urged them to mercy, but they wronged themselves and failed.
TABATABAI:6:128/r3.anchor: بل الله سبحانه غني عنهم لا حاجة له إلى شيء مما بأيديهم حتى يظلمهم لأجله

TABATABAI:6:128/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128/r4.claim: Istakthara min means to do much of a thing or action; the jinn's taking much from humanity refers to their seduction and authority, not to physically bringing humans together, whom God creates and gathers.
TABATABAI:6:128/r4.anchor: يقال أكثر من الشيء أو الفعل واستكثر منه إذا أتى بالكثير

TABATABAI:6:128/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128/r5.claim: The jinn's ‘many’ are people over whom they exert influence through guardianship and seduction, not human bodies they gathered.
TABATABAI:6:128/r5.anchor: وإنما للشياطين الاستكثار مما هم مسلطون عليه وهو إغواء الإنس من طريق ولايتهم عليهم

TABATABAI:6:128/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128/r6.claim: Their mutual guardianship is a voluntary exchange: followers seek benefits from the leader, while leaders seek advantage in managing their followers; neither side is compelled.
TABATABAI:6:128/r6.anchor: وليست بولاية إجبار واضطرار بل من قبيل التعامل من الطرفين يتبع التابع المتبوع ابتغاء لما يرى في اتباعه من الفائدة

TABATABAI:6:128/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128/r7.claim: Jinn enjoy tempting and ruling humans; humans enjoy following whispers and suggestions to obtain material pleasures and satisfy their desires.
TABATABAI:6:128/r7.anchor: فللجن نوع التذاذ من إغواء الإنس والولاية عليهم

TABATABAI:6:128/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128/r8.claim: The human followers enjoyed worldly ornament and desires through Satanic suggestions, while the jinn enjoyed the humans' obedience to their whispers.
TABATABAI:6:128/r8.anchor: فتمتعنا بوساوسهم وتسويلاتهم من متاع الدنيا وزخارفها

TABATABAI:6:128/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128/r9.claim: The appointed term means the limit and degree attained through their deeds—the final level of their actualized existence—not the time their lifespans end; by choosing mutual enjoyment they reached a sinful, unbelieving state.
TABATABAI:6:128/r9.anchor: الحد الذي قدر لوجودهم والدرجة التي حصلت لهم من أعمالهم دون الوقت الذي ينتهي إليه أعمارهم

TABATABAI:6:128/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128/r10.claim: The context may indicate that ‘jinn’ here refers specifically to the devils among the jinn who whisper into people's breasts.
TABATABAI:6:128/r10.anchor: وإنما للشياطين الاستكثار مما هم مسلطون عليه

TABATABAI:6:128-130/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128-130/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128-130/r1.claim: Mathwa is a place of settled residence, from thawa, to remain; ‘the Fire is your abode’ therefore means a settled place from which they will not leave, reinforced by ‘abiding forever.’
TABATABAI:6:128-130/r1.anchor: والمثوى اسم مكان من قولهم ثوى يثوي ثواء أي أقام مع استقرار

TABATABAI:6:128-130/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128-130/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128-130/r2.claim: The exception preserves God's power to take them out of the Fire even though He will not do so.
TABATABAI:6:128-130/r2.anchor: استثناء يفيد أن القدرة الإلهية باقية مع ذلك على ما كانت فله مع ذلك أن يخرجكم منها وإن كان لا يفعل

TABATABAI:6:128-130/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:128-130/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:128-130/r3.claim: The ending that God is Wise and Knowing explains the judgment stated in the verse; the address is to the Prophet.
TABATABAI:6:128-130/r3.anchor: وهو يفيد تعليل البيان الواقع في الآية والخطاب للنبي

TABRISI:6:128-129/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129/r1.speaker: حفص وروح
TABRISI:6:128-129/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ and Rawḥ read 'the day He gathers them' with yāʾ; the remaining readers use nūn, with the cited verse supporting the nūn form.
TABRISI:6:128-129/r1.anchor: قرأ حفص وروح ويوم يحشرهم بالياء والباقون بالنون

TABRISI:6:128-129/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129/r2.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:6:128-129/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses khālidīn as an accusative circumstantial; the fire is their abode while they remain eternally there.
TABRISI:6:128-129/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: خالدين فيها منصوب على الحال

TABRISI:6:128-129/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:6:128-129/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī takes mathwā as a verbal noun, not a place noun, because the construction has a governed circumstantial; the sense is that the fire is your enduring stay, with the pronoun as semantic subject.
TABRISI:6:128-129/r3.anchor: المثوى عندي في الآية اسم للمصدر دون المكان

TABRISI:6:128-129/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:128-129/r4.claim: The verse turns from what precedes to the gathering of all creatures. Other views restrict the gathering to humans and jinn because their exchange follows, or to unbelievers; the day is governed by an implicit 'He says.'
TABRISI:6:128-129/r4.anchor: وقيل: الإنس والجن لأنه يتعقبه حديثهم

TABRISI:6:128-129/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129/r5.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:6:128-129/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the jinn as having greatly multiplied those humans whom they led astray; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses this as misleading and luring humans.
TABRISI:6:128-129/r5.anchor: قد استكثرتم ممن أضللتموه من الإنس عن الزجاج

TABRISI:6:128-129/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:128-129/r6.claim: One explanation: humans took jinn as leaders and followed their desires, while humans enjoyed the pleasures and sensual appetites the jinn adorned for them.
TABRISI:6:128-129/r6.anchor: أن اتخذهم الإنس قادة ورؤساء فاتبعوا أهواءهم

TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r1.speaker: الحسن وابن جريج والزجاج
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r1.claim: Another explanation concerns humans seeking refuge from jinn: travelers called on the lord of a valley, believing the jinn would protect them; the jinn in turn took pleasure and benefit in being believed able to help or harm.
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r1.anchor: واستمتاع الجن بالإنس أن الجن إذا اعتقدوا أن الإنس يتعوذون بهم

TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r2.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says the mutual enjoyment means that each side obeyed and agreed with the other.
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r2.anchor: أن المراد بالاستمتاع طاعة بعضهم لبعض وموافقة بعضهم بعضا عن محمد بن كعب

TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r3.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r3.claim: Al-Balkhī allows that enjoyment is restricted to humans: people enjoyed one another, without the jinn included as participants.
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r3.anchor: قال البلخي: ويحتمل أن يكون الاستمتاع مقصورا عن الإنس

TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r4.speaker: الحسن والسدي
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Suddī take the appointed term as death.
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r4.anchor: يعني بالأجل الموت عن الحسن والسدي

TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r5.speaker: قول غير مسمى
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r5.claim: Another view takes the appointed term as resurrection and gathering: resurrection is the term for requital, just as death is the term for making up what passed.
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: البعث والحشر لأن الحشر أجل الجزاء

TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r6.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r6.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues that the verse implies one lifespan: if there were two terms, someone killed before dying naturally would not have reached his term, yet they say they reached it.
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r6.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه لا أجل إلا واحد لأنه لو كان أجلان

TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r7.speaker: علي بن عيسى وغيره من البغداديين
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r7.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā and other Baghdādī theologians reject that inference: the verse does not rule out separate terms for death and resurrection, or for death and a possible full lifespan.
TABRISI:6:128-129#2/r7.anchor: من البغداديين لا دلالة في الآية على ذلك

TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r1.claim: God says the fire is their abode: they will remain there forever under punishment, subject to the stated exception.

TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the threat against unbelievers was initially open-ended, then made definite by the verse declaring that God does not forgive associating partners.
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r2.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال كان وعيد الكفار مبهما غير مقطوع به

TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes the exception to cover the interval from resurrection through gathering and judgment, or the additional punishment God wills.
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r3.anchor: وثانيها: أن الاستثناء إنما هو من القيامة

TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r4.claim: Another view makes the exception about sinful Muslims, whom God may punish justly according to their deserts or forgive by grace.
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r4.anchor: الاستثناء راجع إلى غير الكفار من عصاة المسلمين الذين هم في مشيئة الله تعالى

TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r5.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ takes the exception to mean those among them who believed.
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r5.anchor: ورابعها: أن معناه إلا ما شاء الله ممن آمن منهم عن عطاء

TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r6.claim: God is wise in his acts and knows everything; another explanation emphasizes that he knows who merits punishment or reward and the measure each merits, and chooses whom to punish or forgive.
TABRISI:6:128-129#3/r6.anchor: أي محكم لأفعاله عليم بكل شيء

THALABI:v4p190/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r1.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v4p190/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says travelers or hunters in desolate land feared the jinn and sought the valley’s master for protection, thereby securing safety from them.
THALABI:v4p190/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: استمتاع الإنس بالجن. هو أن الرجل إذا سافر أو خرج فمشى بأرض قفر

THALABI:v4p190/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r2.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v4p190/r2.claim: The jinn enjoyed this arrangement by boasting that humans sought their protection, increasing their status among their own people.
THALABI:v4p190/r2.anchor: واستمتاع الجن بالإنس هو أن قالوا: قد سدنا الإنس مع الجن حتى عاذوا بنا فيزدادون شرفا

THALABI:v4p190/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب وعبد العزيز بن يحيى
THALABI:v4p190/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb and Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya interpret mutual enjoyment as each side obeying and accommodating the other.
THALABI:v4p190/r3.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب وعبد العزيز بن يحيى: هو طاعة بعضهم بعضا وموافقة بعضهم بعضا

THALABI:v4p190/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p190/r4.claim: Another view is that people benefited from the jinn’s rumors, magic, and soothsaying, while the jinn enjoyed enticing humans to follow them.
THALABI:v4p190/r4.anchor: وقيل: استمتاع الإنس بالجن بما كانوا يأتون إليهم. من الأراجيف والسحر والكهانة،

THALABI:v4p190/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p190/r5.claim: Their appointed term is death and resurrection.
THALABI:v4p190/r5.anchor: وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا يعني الموت والبعث.

THALABI:v4p190/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p190/r6.claim: One explanation takes the exception as the interval between resurrection and entry into Hell.
THALABI:v4p190/r6.anchor: يعني قدر مدة ما بين بعثهم إلى دخولهم جهنم. قال ابن عباس:

THALABI:v4p190/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p190/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the exception prevents anyone from deciding on God’s behalf which creature belongs in Paradise or Hell.
THALABI:v4p190/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذا الاستثناء هو أنه لا ينبغي لأحد أن يحكم على الله في خلقه

THALABI:v4p190/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r8.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v4p190/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi says what God wills is forever.
THALABI:v4p190/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي: إلا ما شاء الله وكان ما شاء الله أبدا.

THALABI:v4p190/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p190/r9.claim: Another interpretation is that the exception refers to kinds of punishment God wills to exclude.
THALABI:v4p190/r9.anchor: وقيل: معناه النار مثواكم خالدين فيها سوى ما شاء الله من أنواع العذاب

THALABI:v4p190/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p190/r10.claim: Another view limits the exception to monotheists whom God will remove from the Fire.
THALABI:v4p190/r10.anchor: وقيل: إلا ما شاء الله من إخراج أهل التوحيد من النار.

THALABI:v4p190/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p190/r11.claim: One view takes the exception as additional punishment God may will for them in Hell.
THALABI:v4p190/r11.anchor: وقيل: إلا ما شاء الله أن يزيدهم من العذاب فيها.

THALABI:v4p190/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p190/r12.claim: Another view refers to their time in this world before punishment.
THALABI:v4p190/r12.anchor: وقيل: إلا ما شاء الله من كونهم في الدنيا بغير عذاب.

THALABI:v4p190/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p190/r13.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v4p190/r13.claim: Ata interprets the exception as those God willed to believe: some believed before the conquest and others after it.
THALABI:v4p190/r13.anchor: وقال عطاء: إلا ما شاء الله من الحق في عمله أن يؤمن فمنهم من آمن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r1.claim: The commentators understand the verse as jinn and humans gathered together at the resurrection's assembly place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬4): (يعني: الجن والإنس يجمعون في موقف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r2.claim: Ata reports Ibn Abbas as identifying those gathered as the jinn and their satan companions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r2.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (يريد: هم وقرناؤهم من الشياطين)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj supplies an implied introductory phrase: they are addressed with, It will be said to them, O company of jinn.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: (المعنى: فيقال لهم: {يا معشر الجن}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Qatada explain the jinn's having taken many humans as their having led them astray through seduction and misguidance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r4.anchor: من إغواء الإنس وإضلالهم، عن ابن عباس (¬8)، والحسن (¬9)، وقتادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r5.claim: In Ibn Abbas's tafsir, the phrase means that the jinn led many humans astray; al-Farra gives the same explanation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as the many people whom the jinn caused to go astray.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq reads it as the many humans whom the jinn misled.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r7.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: ({قد استكثرتم} ممن أضللتموه من الإنس)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r8.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r8.claim: Another commentator states explicitly that the jinn gained many humans through seduction and misguidance; al-Wahidi says the explanations amount to the same thing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r8.anchor: وقال غيره: ({قد استكثرتم من الإنس} بالإغواء والإضلال)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p434/r9.claim: The humans called the jinn's allies are the people whom the jinn led astray.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r1.speaker: الحسن وابن جريج والكلبي وعكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r1.claim: These authorities describe humans seeking a valley jinn's protection while traveling in desolate country; humans gain safety, while jinn gain the honor of being treated as powerful protectors.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r1.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن (¬3) وابن جريج (¬4)، والكلبي (¬5)، وعكرمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r2.speaker: الحسن وابن جريج والكلبي وعكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r2.claim: In this account, a jinn boasts that humans and jinn have submitted to him, since a human has acknowledged his ability to protect him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r2.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن (¬3) وابن جريج (¬4)، والكلبي (¬5)، وعكرمة (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r3.speaker: الحسن وابن جريج والكلبي وعكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r3.claim: They cite 72:6 as evidence for humans seeking refuge with jinn.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r3.anchor: واحتجوا على هذا بقوله تعالى: {وأنه كان رجال من الإنس يعوذون برجال من الجن}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata's report, says the mutual enjoyment occurred in worldly life and involved the jinn leading humans astray.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: {ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض}: (يريد: في الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r5.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r5.claim: On this explanation, jinn enjoyed human obedience to their calls toward error, unbelief, and sins; humans enjoyed jinn's beautifying desired acts and making them easier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r5.anchor: أن استمتاع الجن بالإنس طاعتهم لهم فيما يغرونهم به من الضلالة والكفر والمعاصي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the mutual-misguidance explanation: the wording points to humans accepting jinn's temptations, and few humans sought refuge with jinn.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p435/r6.anchor: اختيار الزجاج؛ لأنه قال: (الذي يدل عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r1.speaker: الحسن والسدي وأكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r1.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Suddi, and most commentators take the appointed term to mean death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r1.anchor: في قول الحسن (¬2) والسدي (¬3)، وأكثر المفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r2.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the appointed term to be resurrection and gathering.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses mathwākum as your place of staying.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says mathwā means abode and khālidīn is an accusative circumstantial qualifier: the Fire is their abode while they remain there eternally.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: (المثوى: المقام، {خالدين فيها} منصوب على الحال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r5.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r5.claim: Abu Ali argues mathwā is a verbal noun, not a place noun, because the following circumstantial phrase operates on it; it means the Fire is your remaining there, with the addressees as semantic agents.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r5.anchor: المثوى عندي في الآية اسم للمصدر دون المكان، لحصول الحال في الكلام معملا فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r6.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r6.claim: Abu Ali adduces poetry where maghār takes an object introduced by ʿalā; this shows it is a verbal noun, while a place noun would not govern an object.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r6.anchor: وما هي إلا في إزار وعلقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r7.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r7.claim: Abu Ali explains time adverbials such as the cited expressions as verbal nouns used by extension after deleting a time noun; their sense of passing suits time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r7.anchor: فهو من باب قولك: أتيتك خفوق النجم، ومقدم الحاج، وخلافة فلان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r8.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r8.claim: Abu Ali notes that Arabic often uses mā with a verb as a time adverbial, and some grammarians call this construction mā of time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r8.anchor: حتى إن قوما من النحويين (¬5) يسمونها ما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r9.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p437/r9.claim: Abu Ali understands the people addressed as those who deserve to dwell and remain eternally in the Fire; Ibn Abbas's gloss of mathwā as a place of staying supports this.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the exception covers people already known by God to accept Islam and believe the Prophet and his message; this requires mā to mean man, those who.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (استثنى الله قوما قد سبق في علمه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq takes the exception from the duration of Judgment Day: it excludes the time spent being raised from graves and being judged before entry into the Fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r2.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (معنى الاستثناء عندي: إنما هو من يوم القيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God decreed faith, repentance, and truthful belief for the excepted people, and knew the goodness, piety, and faith in their hearts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r3.anchor: حكم للذين استثنى بالتصديق والتوبة وعلم ما في قلوبهم من البر والتقوى والإيمان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r4.claim: The people of meaning read the passage as a warning against jinn tempting people and making evil attractive, since the jinn and their human allies will be paired in the Fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p440/r4.anchor: معنى هذه الآية: التحذير من إغواء الجن تزيينهم القبيح، فإنهم يقرنون مع أوليائهم من الإنس في النار

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p160#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p160#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p160#2/r1.claim: The jinn's having much of humankind means they led many people astray.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p160#2/r1.anchor: يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الإنس} أي: أضللتم كثيرا منهم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p160#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p160#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p160#2/r2.claim: Each side took a share or benefit from the other.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p160#2/r2.anchor: وقال أولياؤهم من الإنس ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض} أي: أخذ كل من كل نصيبا (1) .

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r4.claim: The jinn greatly increased their influence over humans by leading them astray.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r4.anchor: { يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الإنس } أي: من إغوائهم وإضلالهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r5.claim: Humans obeyed the jinn and accepted their delusions; the jinn made human desires attractive and easy to fulfill.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r5.anchor: { وقال أولياؤهم } الذين أضلهم الجن { من الإنس ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض } يعني: طاعة الإنس للجن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r6.claim: The term means death; apparently it means resurrection and gathering.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r6.anchor: { وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا } يعني: الموت، والظاهر أنه البعث والحشر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r7.claim: The fire is their dwelling; those excepted are people God already knew would submit.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r7.anchor: { قال النار مثواكم } فيها مقامكم { خالدين فيها إلا ما شاء الله } من شاء الله، وهم من سبق في علم الله أنهم يسلمون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r8.claim: God decreed repentance and truth for those excepted and knows the goodness in their hearts.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:126-128/r8.anchor: { إن ربك حكيم } حكم للذين استثنى بالتوبة والتصديق { عليم } علم ما في قلوبهم من البر.

ELMALILI:6:128-129/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r1.claim: A future day will bring all humans and jinn together for judgment.
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r1.anchor: Düşün ki bir gün gelecek Allah o ins ü cinnin hepsini bir yere toplayacak;

ELMALILI:6:128-129/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r2.claim: The address to the jinn assembly is glossed as addressing hidden devil societies that targeted and misled many humans, swelling their own company by drawing people into the devils’ ranks.
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r2.anchor: ey ma‘şer-i cin, ey cin cemaati, ey gizli şeytan cemiyetleri; insten çoğuna göz diktiniz, çok iğvâ ve idlâl ettiniz

ELMALILI:6:128-129/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r3.claim: The human allies are rendered as the jinn’s yardakları, their henchmen or followers.

ELMALILI:6:128-129/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r4.claim: Jinn taught people routes to lust, deception, fraud, false reports, magic, and ways to spread corruption and hide; people gained pleasures, while jinn gained their aims through people’s willing acceptance and assistance.
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r4.anchor: Cinler inse şehevât yollarını ve vesâitini gösterdiler, mekr ü hud‘a, tezvir ve erâcif, sihr ü efsun usullerini

ELMALILI:6:128-129/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r5.claim: The humans’ willing acceptance and help mean responsibility belongs not only to their jinn companions; both sides benefited and share culpability.
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r5.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh bu babda mes’ûliyet yalnız cin dostlarımızın değildir. Doğrusu biz yekdiğerimizden istifade ettik

ELMALILI:6:128-129/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r6.claim: The human allies admit reaching the end of the respite God appointed for them, confessing their sins and their shared responsibility with the jinn.
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r6.anchor: ve bizim için tâyin ve tesmiye ettiğin ecelimize yettik; bize verdiği mühletin nihâyetine erdik.

ELMALILI:6:128-129/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r7.claim: He identifies the appointed term with the specified term mentioned at the sūra’s beginning and says that the appointed endpoint, the Day of Resurrection, has arrived.
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r7.anchor: sûrenin başında وَأَجَلٌۭ مُّسَمًّى عِندَهُۥ ثُمَّ أَنتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ [6/2] diye beyan olunan ecel-i müsemmâ

ELMALILI:6:128-129/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r8.claim: Because the exception says “what God wills” rather than “whom God wills,” he takes it to refer to periods of time, not particular people, within the promise of eternal residence in Hell.
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r8.anchor: hulûd-ı nârdan bu istisnâ bazı eşhâsa değil, bazı ezmâna aittir.

ELMALILI:6:128-129/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r9.claim: He says that in certain periods unbelievers will be taken from the fire, cast into the cold of zamharir, and then returned to the fire.
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r9.anchor: Allah’ın dilediği bazı zamanlar küffâr ateşten çıkarılıp soğuğa, zemherîre atılacak, sonra yine nâra iade olunacaktır.

ELMALILI:6:128-129/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r10.claim: God perfectly orders His acts and knows the hidden and manifest states of all humans and jinn and the punishments they deserve; He judges with knowledge and will.
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r10.anchor: ins ü cin bütün sekaleynin de gizli açık bütün hâllerini ve lâyık oldukları cezâları bilir.

ELMALILI:6:128-129/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r13.claim: When the jinn give no answer to the rebuke for misleading humans, their human allies step forward to excuse them, then confess mutual benefit and shared guilt.
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r13.anchor: cin hiçbir cevap vermediği hâlde onların insten olan dostları, dostlukları muktezâsınca ortaya atılarak mes’ûliyeti üzerlerine alarak

ELMALILI:6:128-129/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r14.claim: The confession shows humans and jinn to be one collective community with the same conscience, deeds, responsibility, and entitlement to the same punishment, rather than separate assemblies.
ELMALILI:6:128-129/r14.anchor: cinnin ayrı, insin ayrı bir ma‘şer değil, hey’et-i mecmû‘asının bir ma‘şer; aynı vicdan, aynı kesb, aynı mes’ûliyet taşıyan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r1.claim: After describing believers guided by God’s explained signs who gain Paradise, the passage depicts the inevitable gathering of polytheists and unbelievers as if already past.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r1.anchor: Önceki âyetler grubunda Allah’ın doğru yola ilettiği, ayrıntılı olarak açıklanan âyetler üzerinde düşünerek onlardan gerekli ders ve öğütleri alan ve bu sayede “esenlik yurdu”nu (cennet) kazanan müminlerin bu güzel âkıbetinden söz edildikten sonra

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r2.claim: The jinn addressed are the jinn-devils mentioned at 6:112, who worked to mislead humans and make them their adherents.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r3.claim: The humans will say they benefited from the devils and the devils from them: demons facilitated their desires and pleasures, while humans increased the demons’ followers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r3.anchor: şeytanlar müşriklerin kötü arzu ve isteklerini kolaylaştırmışlar, zevklerin ve hazların kapılarını açmışlar; onlara şeytanlara bağlanmak suretiyle onların yandaşlarının sayılarını çoğaltmışlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r4.claim: The verse portrays an enduring, deep alliance between instigators of evil and unbelievers, with responsibility voluntarily shared across generations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r4.anchor: Âyetin bu kısmı kötülük âmilleri olan şeytanlarla inkârcılar arasında her devirde geçerli ve sorumluluğu gönüllü paylaşacak kadar ileri olan derin bir ilişkiyi dile getirmesi bakımından ilgi çekicidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r5.claim: Their admission that the appointed term has arrived confesses that their respite is over and no option but submission remains; it comes too late to help.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r5.anchor: “Bize verdiğin sürenin sonuna ulaştık” şeklindeki ifadeleri, artık mühletlerinin dolduğunu, Allah’a teslim olmaktan başka çıkar yolları bulunmadığını gösteren samimi bir itiraftır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r6.claim: God answers that the Fire will be their eternal home, and their belated confession cannot avert the judgment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r6.anchor: Ne var ki geç kalmış bu itiraf işe yaramayacak ve Allah Teâlâ onlara “İçinde ebedî kalacağınız yer ateştir” buyuracaktır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r7.claim: One interpretation takes the exception to mean that God may end the Fire’s eternity after a period.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r7.anchor: Bir görüşe göre bu, “Allah dilerse bu ebedîliği bir müddet sonra sona erdirir”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r8.claim: Another interpretation says God may spare selected people from remaining eternally in Hell; this, too, implies either finite Hell or exceptions among disbelievers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r8.anchor: başka bir görüşe göre de “Allah, dilediği kimseleri orada ebedî kalmaktan kurtarır” anlamına gelir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r9.claim: Because other verses rule out both implications, the author prefers that the exception mean God is not compelled to keep people in Hell forever; it is his free will, as 11:107 confirms.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:128/r9.anchor: Bu sebeple söz konusu istisnayı, bazı insanları sürekli olarak cehennemde bırakmanın, Allah için bir mecburiyet olmadığı, O’nun hür irade ve isteği ile olduğu şeklinde anlamak daha isabetli görülmüştür.
